Article 730 Where the parties have not agreed on the lease term or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the lease shall be deemed to be a lease for an indefinite term; the parties may dissolve the contract at any time, provided that they shall notify the other party within a reasonable period in advance.

Article 731 Where the leased property endangers the safety or health of the lessee, the lessee may dissolve the contract at any time even if the lessee knew at the time of concluding the contract that the leased property was substandard.

Article 732 Where the lessee dies during the term of the house lease, the persons who lived together with the lessee during its lifetime or its joint operators may lease the house in accordance with the original lease contract.

Article 733 Upon expiration of the lease term, the lessee shall return the leased property. The returned leased property shall be in a condition consistent with that resulting from its use in accordance with the agreement or the nature of the leased property.

Article 734 Where the lessee continues to use the leased property after the expiration of the lease term and the lessor raises no objection, the original lease contract shall remain valid, but the lease term shall be deemed indefinite.
Upon expiration of the lease term, the lessee of the house has the right of first refusal to lease the house on the same conditions.

Article 735 A financial leasing contract is a contract whereby the lessor, based on the lessee's selection of the seller and the leased property, purchases the leased property from the seller, provides it to the lessee for use, and the lessee pays the rent.

Article 736 The contents of a financial leasing contract generally include clauses on the name, quantity, specifications, technical performance, and inspection method of the leased property, the lease term, the composition of the rent and the term and method and currency of payment, and the ownership of the leased property upon expiration of the lease term.
A financial leasing contract shall be in written form.
Article 737 Where the parties conclude a financial leasing contract by fabricating the leased property, the contract is void.

Article 738 Where an administrative license is required for the operation and use of the leased property in accordance with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, the lessor's failure to obtain the administrative license shall not affect the validity of the financial leasing contract.

Article 739 Where the lessor concludes a sales contract based on the lessee's selection of the seller and the leased property, the seller shall deliver the subject matter to the lessee in accordance with the agreement, and the lessee enjoys the buyer's rights related to taking delivery of the subject matter.

Article 740 Where the seller violates the obligation to deliver the subject matter to the lessee, under any of the following circumstances, the lessee may refuse to take delivery of the subject matter delivered by the seller:
(1) the subject matter materially fails to conform to the agreement;
(2) the subject matter is not delivered in accordance with the agreement, and is still not delivered within a reasonable period after being urged by the lessee or lessor.
Where the lessee refuses to take delivery of the subject matter, it shall promptly notify the lessor.

Article 741 The lessor, seller, and lessee may agree that, if the seller fails to perform its obligations under the sales contract, the lessee shall exercise the right to claim compensation. Where the lessee exercises the right to claim compensation, the lessor shall provide assistance.

Article 742 The lessee's exercise of the right to claim compensation against the seller shall not affect its obligation to pay the rent. However, if the lessee determined the leased object relying on the lessor's expertise or the lessor interfered with the selection of the leased object, the lessee may request a reduction or exemption of the corresponding rent.

Article 743 Where the lessor falls under any of the following circumstances, thereby causing the lessee to fail in exercising the right to claim compensation against the seller, the lessee shall have the right to request the lessor to assume the corresponding liability:
(1) The lessor knew of a quality defect in the leased object but failed to inform the lessee; or
(2) The lessor failed to provide necessary assistance in a timely manner when the lessee exercised the right to claim compensation.
Where the lessor is dilatory in exercising a right to claim compensation against the seller that only the lessor can exercise, thereby causing losses to the lessee, the lessee shall have the right to request the lessor to assume liability for compensation.

Article 744 Where a sales contract is concluded by the lessor in accordance with the lessee's selection of the seller and the leased object, the lessor shall not modify the contents of the contract that are related to the lessee without the lessee's consent.
Article 745 The lessor's ownership of the leased object shall not be set up against a bona fide third party if it is not registered.

Article 746 Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the rent under a financial leasing contract shall be determined based on most or all of the cost of purchasing the leased object and the lessor's reasonable profit.

Article 747 The lessor shall not be liable if the leased object does not conform to the agreement or the intended purpose, unless the lessee determined the leased object relying on the lessor's expertise or the lessor interfered with the selection of the leased object.
Article 749 During the period when the lessee possesses the leased object, the lessor shall not be liable for personal injury or property damage caused to a third party by the leased object.

Article 750 The lessee shall properly keep and use the leased object.
The lessee shall perform the obligation of maintaining the leased object during the period of possession.

Article 751 Where the leased object is damaged or destroyed during the period when the lessee is in possession thereof, the lessor shall have the right to request the lessee to continue paying the rent, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 752 The lessee shall pay the rent in accordance with the agreement. If the lessee still fails to pay the rent within a reasonable period after receiving a demand, the lessor may request the payment of the entire rent, or may rescind the contract and take back the leased object.

Article 753 Where the lessee transfers, mortgages, pledges, makes a capital contribution with, or otherwise disposes of the leased object without the lessor's consent, the lessor may rescind the financial leasing contract.

Article 754 The lessor or the lessee may rescind a financial leasing contract in any of the following circumstances:
(1) The sales contract concluded between the lessor and the seller is rescinded, confirmed as void, or revoked, and no new sales contract can be concluded;
(2) The leased object is damaged or destroyed for reasons not attributable to the parties, and it cannot be repaired or a substitute cannot be determined; or
(3) The purpose of the financial leasing contract cannot be achieved due to reasons attributable to the seller.

Article 755 Where a financial leasing contract is rescinded because the sales contract is rescinded, confirmed as void, or revoked, and the seller and the leased object were selected by the lessee, the lessor shall have the right to request the lessee to compensate for the corresponding losses, unless the sales contract was rescinded, confirmed as void, or revoked due to reasons attributable to the lessor.
Where the lessor's losses have already been compensated at the time the sales contract was rescinded, confirmed as void, or revoked, the lessee shall no longer bear the corresponding compensation liability.

Article 756 Where a financial leasing contract is rescinded due to reasons not attributable to the parties, such as accidental damage or destruction of the leased object after delivery to the lessee, the lessor may request the lessee to provide compensation based on the depreciation of the leased object.

Article 757 The lessor and the lessee may agree on the ownership of the leased object upon expiration of the lease term. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and the ownership cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the ownership of the leased object shall belong to the lessor.

Article 758 Where the parties agree that the leased object shall belong to the lessee upon expiration of the lease term, and the lessee has paid most of the rent but is unable to pay the remaining rent, and the lessor rescinds the contract and takes back the leased object, if the value of the repossessed leased object exceeds the rent and other fees owed by the lessee, the lessee may request a corresponding refund.
Where the parties agree that the leased object shall belong to the lessor upon expiration of the lease term, and the lessee is unable to return the leased object because it has been damaged, destroyed, or has become attached to or commingled with another object, the lessor shall have the right to request the lessee to provide reasonable compensation.

Article 759 Where the parties agree that, upon expiration of the lease term, the lessee only needs to pay a symbolic price to the lessor, the ownership of the leased object shall be deemed to belong to the lessee upon the fulfillment of the agreed rent obligation.

Article 760 Where a financial leasing contract is invalid, the ownership of the leased object under such circumstance shall follow any agreement between the parties. In the absence of an agreement or if the agreement is unclear, the leased object shall be returned to the lessor. However, if the contract is invalid due to reasons attributable to the lessee, and the lessor does not request the return or the return would significantly reduce the utility of the leased object, the ownership of the leased object shall belong to the lessee, and the lessee shall provide reasonable compensation to the lessor.

Article 761 A factoring contract is a contract under which an accounts receivable creditor assigns its existing or future accounts receivable to a factor, and the factor provides services such as financing, management or collection of accounts receivable, or guarantee of payment by the accounts receivable debtor.

Article 762 The content of a factoring contract generally includes clauses such as the type of business, scope of services, term of services, status of the underlying transaction contract, information on the accounts receivable, the factoring financing funds or service remuneration and payment method thereof.
A factoring contract shall be in writing.

Article 763 Where an accounts receivable creditor and its debtor fabricate accounts receivable as the subject of assignment and enter into a factoring contract with a factor, the accounts receivable debtor shall not assert against the factor that the accounts receivable do not exist, unless the factor knew of such fabrication.
Article 764 Where a factor sends a notice of assignment of accounts receivable to the accounts receivable debtor, it shall identify itself as a factor and attach the necessary supporting documents.

Article 765 After the accounts receivable debtor receives the notice of assignment of accounts receivable, if the accounts receivable creditor and the debtor negotiate to modify or terminate the underlying transaction contract without justifiable cause, thereby adversely affecting the factor, such modification or termination shall not be binding on the factor.

Article 766 Where the parties agree on factoring with recourse, the factor may claim repayment of the principal and interest of the factoring financing or repurchase of the accounts receivable claim from the accounts receivable creditor, and may also claim the accounts receivable claim from the accounts receivable debtor. If, after the factor claims the accounts receivable claim from the accounts receivable debtor and deducts the principal and interest of the factoring financing and related expenses, there is a surplus, the surplus shall be returned to the accounts receivable creditor.

Article 767 Where the parties agree on factoring without recourse, the factor shall claim the accounts receivable claim from the accounts receivable debtor, and the factor is not required to return to the accounts receivable creditor any amount it receives in excess of the principal and interest of the factoring financing and related expenses.

Article 768 Where an accounts receivable creditor enters into multiple factoring contracts for the same accounts receivable, causing multiple factors to claim rights, a factor that has registered shall have priority over an unregistered factor in obtaining the accounts receivable; where all factors have registered, they shall obtain the accounts receivable in the order of registration time; where none have registered, the factor named in the notice of assignment that first reaches the accounts receivable debtor shall obtain the accounts receivable; where neither registration nor notice has occurred, the factors shall obtain the accounts receivable in proportion to the factoring financing funds or service remuneration.
Article 769 Matters not covered in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions in Chapter 6 of this Part on the assignment of claims.

Article 770 A work contract is a contract under which a contractor completes work in accordance with the requirements of the client and delivers the work product, and the client pays remuneration.
Work includes processing, manufacturing, repairing, reproducing, testing, inspecting, and similar activities.

Article 771 The content of a work contract generally includes clauses such as the subject matter, quantity, quality, remuneration of the work, the method of performance, the provision of materials, the time limit for performance, and the standards and methods for acceptance inspection.

Article 772 A contractor shall complete the principal work with its own equipment, technology, and labor, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Where the contractor entrusts the principal work it has contracted to a third party, it shall be liable to the client for the work product completed by that third party; if the client does not consent to such entrustment, the client may also dissolve the contract.

Article 773 A contractor may entrust the ancillary work it has contracted to a third party. Where the contractor entrusts the ancillary work it has contracted to a third party, it shall be liable to the client for the work product completed by that third party.
Article 774 Where the contractor provides materials, it shall select and use the materials in accordance with the agreement, and shall submit to inspection by the client.

Article 775 Where the client provides materials, it shall provide them in accordance with the agreement. The contractor shall promptly inspect the materials provided by the client, and if it finds them non-conforming with the agreement, it shall promptly notify the client to replace, supplement, or take other remedial measures.
The contractor shall not replace, without authorization, the materials provided by the client, nor shall it replace parts that do not require repair.

Article 776 Where the contractor discovers that the drawings or technical requirements provided by the client are unreasonable, it shall promptly notify the client. If the client's failure to respond or other reasons cause losses to the contractor, the client shall compensate for such losses.
Article 777 Where the client changes the requirements for the work during its performance, causing losses to the contractor, the client shall compensate for such losses.

Article 778 Where the work requires the client's assistance, the client has a duty to assist. If the client fails to perform its duty of assistance, causing the work to be impossible to complete, the contractor may demand that the client perform its duty within a reasonable time limit, and may extend the time limit for performance; if the client fails to perform within the extended period, the contractor may dissolve the contract.

Article 779 During the performance of the work, the contractor shall accept the necessary supervision and inspection by the client. The client shall not hinder the contractor's normal work due to such supervision and inspection.

Article 780 Upon completion of the work, the contractor shall deliver the work product to the client and submit the necessary technical documents and relevant quality certificates. The client shall accept and inspect the work product.

Article 781 Where the work product delivered by the contractor does not meet the quality requirements, the client may reasonably choose to request the contractor to bear liability for breach of contract such as repair, rework, reduction of remuneration, and compensation for losses.

Article 782 The client shall pay the remuneration within the agreed period. Where there is no agreement or the agreement on the period for payment of remuneration is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the client shall pay the remuneration upon delivery of the work product by the contractor; where the work product is delivered in part, the client shall make proportionate payment.

Article 783 Where the client fails to pay the contractor the remuneration or material costs or other equivalent amounts, the contractor shall have a lien on the completed work product or the right to refuse delivery, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 784 The contractor shall properly keep the materials provided by the client and the completed work product, and shall bear liability for compensation for any damage or loss caused by improper keeping.
Article 785 The contractor shall keep the secrets according to the requirements of the client, and shall not retain copies or technical materials without the permission of the client.
Article 786 Co-contractors shall bear joint and several liability to the client, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Article 787 The client may rescind the contract at any time before the contractor completes the work, but shall compensate the contractor for any losses caused thereby.

Article 788 A construction project contract is a contract whereby the contractor undertakes the construction of a project and the contractee pays the price.
Construction project contracts include contracts for survey, design, and construction of projects.
Article 789 A construction project contract shall be in writing.
Article 790 The tendering and bidding activities for construction projects shall be conducted openly, fairly, and impartially in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.

Article 791 The contractee may enter into a construction project contract with a general contractor, or may enter into separate contracts for survey, design, and construction with the surveyor, designer, and constructor. The contractee shall not divide a construction project that should be completed by one contractor into several parts and contract them out to several contractors.
With the consent of the contractee, the general contractor or the survey, design, or construction contractor may subcontract part of its contracted work to a third party. The third party shall bear joint and several liability to the contractee with the general contractor or the survey, design, or construction contractor for the work product it completes. The contractor shall not subcontract the entire construction project it has contracted to a third party, nor shall it divide the entire construction project it has contracted and subcontract it in the name of subcontracting.
Contractors are prohibited from subcontracting projects to entities that do not possess corresponding qualifications. Subcontracting units are prohibited from re-subcontracting the projects they have contracted. The construction of the main structure of a construction project must be completed by the contractor itself.

Article 792 Contracts for major national construction projects shall be entered into in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the State and documents such as the investment plan approved by the State and the feasibility study report.

Article 793 Where a construction project construction contract is void, but the construction project has passed acceptance inspection, the contractor may be compensated by a discounted amount with reference to the agreement on project price in the contract.
Where a construction project construction contract is void and the construction project has failed the acceptance inspection, the matter shall be handled as follows:
(1) if the construction project passes the acceptance inspection after repair, the contractee may request the contractor to bear the repair costs;
(2) if the construction project fails the acceptance inspection after repair, the contractor shall have no right to request compensation by a discounted amount with reference to the agreement on project price in the contract.
Where the contractee is at fault for losses caused by the construction project failing to meet the standards, it shall bear corresponding liability.

Article 794 The content of a survey or design contract generally includes clauses such as the time limit for submitting relevant basic data and documents such as budgetary estimates and final accounts, quality requirements, fees, and other conditions for cooperation.

Article 795 The content of a construction contract generally includes clauses such as the scope of the project, construction period, commencement and completion times of intermediate handover works, project quality, project cost, time for delivery of technical data, responsibility for supply of materials and equipment, disbursement and settlement, completion acceptance, scope and period of quality warranty, and mutual cooperation.

Article 796 Where supervision is implemented for a construction project, the contractee shall enter into a commission supervision contract in writing with the supervisor. The rights, obligations, and legal liabilities of the contractee and the supervisor shall be governed by the provisions of this Part on commission contracts and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 797 The contractee may, without hindering the normal operation of the contractor, inspect the progress and quality of the work at any time.

Article 798 Before a concealed project is covered, the contractor shall notify the contractee for inspection. If the contractee fails to conduct the inspection in a timely manner, the contractor may extend the project period and has the right to request compensation for losses such as work stoppage and idle labor.

Article 799 After the completion of a construction project, the contractee shall promptly conduct acceptance inspection in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications, the construction acceptance standards issued by the State, and the quality inspection standards. If the project passes the acceptance inspection, the contractee shall pay the price in accordance with the agreement and take delivery of the construction project.
A completed construction project may be delivered for use only after it passes the acceptance inspection; it shall not be delivered for use if no acceptance inspection has been conducted or the inspection has been failed.

Article 800 Where the quality of the survey or design fails to meet the requirements, or the survey or design documents are not submitted within the time limit, delaying the project schedule and causing losses to the contractee, the surveyor or designer shall continue to perfect the survey or design, reduce or waive the survey or design fees, and compensate for the losses.

Article 801 If the quality of a construction project fails to meet the agreed standards due to the constructor's fault, the contractee shall have the right to request the constructor to repair, redo, or modify the work free of charge within a reasonable period. If the project is delivered late after such repair, redoing, or modification, the constructor shall bear liability for breach of contract.
Article 802 If, due to the contractor's fault, a construction project causes personal injury or property damage within its reasonable service life, the contractor shall bear compensation liability.

Article 803 If the contractee fails to provide raw materials, equipment, site, funds, or technical data as agreed in terms of time and requirements, the contractor may extend the construction period and shall have the right to claim compensation for losses such as work stoppage or idle labor.

Article 804 If, due to the contractee's fault, a project is suspended or postponed midway, the contractee shall take measures to remedy or mitigate the losses and compensate the contractor for losses and actual expenses incurred thereby, including work stoppage, idle labor, re-handling, relocation of machinery and equipment, and accumulation of materials and components.

Article 805 If, due to the contractee's changes in plan, inaccuracy of provided materials, or failure to provide necessary conditions for survey and design work within the time limit, the survey or design work is redone, suspended, or modified, the contractee shall pay additional fees based on the actual workload consumed by the surveyor or designer.

Article 806 If the contractor subcontracts or illegally sublets the construction project, the contractee may rescind the contract.
If the contractee provides main construction materials, building components, or equipment that do not conform to mandatory standards or fails to perform its obligation of assistance, rendering the contractor unable to proceed with construction, and the contractee still fails to perform the corresponding obligations within a reasonable period after being urged, the contractor may rescind the contract.
After the contract is rescinded, if the quality of the completed part of the construction project is up to standard, the contractee shall pay the corresponding project price as agreed; if the quality of the completed part is not up to standard, the matter shall be handled by reference to Article 793 of this Law.

Article 807 If the contractee fails to pay the price as agreed, the contractor may urge the contractee to pay the price within a reasonable period. If the contractee fails to pay within the extended period, the contractor may, unless the nature of the construction project makes it unsuitable for appraisal or auction, negotiate with the contractee to appraise the project or request the People's Court to auction the project according to law. The price for the construction project shall be satisfied on a priority basis from the proceeds of the appraisal or auction.
Article 808 Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions on work contracts.

Article 809 A transport contract is a contract whereby the carrier transports a passenger or cargo from the place of departure to the agreed destination, and the passenger, consignor, or consignee pays the fare or freight charges.
Article 810 A carrier engaged in public transport shall not refuse the normal and reasonable transport requests of passengers or consignors.
Article 811 The carrier shall transport the passenger or cargo safely to the agreed destination within the agreed period or a reasonable period.
Article 812 The carrier shall transport the passenger or cargo to the agreed destination via the agreed or customary transport route.

Article 813 The passenger, consignor, or consignee shall pay the fare or freight charges. If, due to the carrier's failure to transport via the agreed or customary route, the fare or freight charges are increased, the passenger, consignor, or consignee may refuse to pay the increased portion.
Article 814 A passenger transport contract is formed when the carrier issues a ticket to the passenger, unless the parties have agreed otherwise or there is a customary practice to the contrary.

Article 815 A passenger shall travel in accordance with the time, flight number, and seat number specified on the valid ticket. If a passenger travels without a ticket, exceeds the destination, upgrades without authorization, or uses a discounted ticket for which they do not qualify, they shall make up the fare, and the carrier may charge an additional fare in accordance with the regulations; if the passenger fails to pay the fare, the carrier may refuse transport.
If a passenger under a real-name passenger transport contract loses their ticket, they may request the carrier to report the loss and reissue the ticket, and the carrier shall not charge the fare again or any other unreasonable fees.

Article 816 If a passenger, for their own reasons, cannot travel at the time specified on the ticket, they shall go through the procedures for refund or change within the agreed period; if they fail to do so within the period, the carrier may refuse to refund the fare and shall no longer be obliged to transport them.

Article 817 The luggage a passenger carries on their person shall comply with the agreed limits and category requirements; if the luggage exceeds the limits or violates the category requirements, the passenger shall go through the consignment procedures.

Article 818 A passenger shall not carry on their person or conceal in their luggage any dangerous or prohibited articles that are flammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, radioactive, or likely to endanger the safety of persons or property on the means of transport.
If a passenger violates the preceding paragraph, the carrier may unload, destroy, or deliver the dangerous or prohibited articles to the relevant authorities. If the passenger insists on carrying or concealing such dangerous or prohibited articles, the carrier shall refuse transport.

Article 819 The carrier shall strictly perform its obligation of safe transport and promptly inform passengers of matters requiring attention for safe transport. Passengers shall actively assist and cooperate with the carrier's reasonable arrangements for safe transport.

Article 820 The carrier shall transport passengers in accordance with the time, flight number, and seat number specified on the valid ticket. If the carrier delays transport or is otherwise unable to provide normal transport, it shall promptly notify and remind passengers, take necessary accommodation measures, and arrange for passengers to change to another flight or provide a refund at their request; if this causes losses to passengers, the carrier shall bear compensation liability, unless the cause is not attributable to the carrier.

Article 821 Where a carrier arbitrarily lowers its service standards, it shall, at the request of the passenger, refund the ticket or reduce the fare; where it raises the service standards, it shall not charge an additional fare.
Article 822 The carrier shall, during the course of transport, use its best endeavors to rescue passengers who are suffering from acute diseases, are in childbirth, or are in danger.

Article 823 The carrier shall bear compensation liability for the personal injury or death of a passenger during the course of transport, except where the injury or death is caused by the passenger's own health condition, or the carrier proves that the injury or death is caused by the passenger's intentional conduct or gross negligence.
The provisions of the preceding paragraph apply to passengers who, in accordance with the applicable provisions, are exempt from a ticket, hold a preferential ticket, or ride without a ticket with the carrier's permission.

Article 824 Where the hand luggage carried by a passenger is damaged or lost during the course of transport, the carrier shall bear compensation liability if it is at fault.
Where the checked luggage of a passenger is damaged or lost, the relevant provisions on the carriage of goods apply.

Article 825 When handling the carriage of goods, the consignor shall accurately inform the carrier of the name or designation of the consignee or the consignee to be notified, the name, nature, weight, and quantity of the goods, the place of receipt, and other necessary information relating to the carriage of goods.
Where the carrier suffers a loss due to the consignor's false declaration or omission of material information, the consignor shall bear compensation liability.

Article 826 Where the carriage of goods requires formalities such as examination and approval or inspection, the consignor shall submit to the carrier the documents evidencing completion of such formalities.

Article 827 The consignor shall package the goods in the agreed manner. Where there is no agreement on the packaging manner or the agreement is unclear, the provisions of Article 619 of this Law apply.
Where the consignor violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the carrier may refuse to transport the goods.

Article 828 Where the consignor consigns dangerous goods such as flammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, or radioactive articles, it shall, in accordance with the relevant state provisions on the transport of dangerous goods, package the dangerous goods properly, affix warning signs and labels for dangerous goods, and submit to the carrier written documents concerning the name, nature, and precautionary measures of the dangerous goods.
Where the consignor violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the carrier may refuse to transport the goods or may take corresponding measures to avoid the occurrence of loss, and the expenses incurred thereby shall be borne by the consignor.

Article 829 Before the carrier delivers the goods to the consignee, the consignor may request the carrier to discontinue the transport, return the goods, change the place of destination, or deliver the goods to another consignee, provided that it shall compensate the carrier for any loss suffered thereby.

Article 830 After the goods have arrived at the place of destination, the carrier that is aware of the consignee shall promptly notify the consignee, and the consignee shall promptly take delivery of the goods. Where the consignee fails to take delivery within the time limit, it shall pay storage fees and other expenses to the carrier.

Article 831 When taking delivery of the goods, the consignee shall inspect the goods within the agreed time limit. Where there is no agreement on the time limit for inspection or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the consignee shall inspect the goods within a reasonable time limit. Where the consignee does not raise any objection to the quantity or damage of the goods within the agreed time limit or within a reasonable time limit, it shall be deemed as prima facie evidence that the carrier has delivered the goods as described in the transport documents.

Article 832 The carrier shall bear compensation liability for the damage or loss of goods during the course of transport. However, the carrier shall not bear compensation liability if it proves that the damage or loss of the goods is caused by force majeure, the natural nature of the goods themselves or reasonable wear and tear, or the fault of the consignor or the consignee.

Article 833 The amount of compensation for the damage or loss of the goods shall be calculated in accordance with the agreement between the parties, if any; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, it shall be calculated based on the market price at the place of destination of the goods at the time of delivery or the time when delivery should have been made. Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise for the method of calculating the amount of compensation and the limitation of liability, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 834 Where two or more carriers operate through transport by the same mode of transport, the carrier that concludes the contract with the consignor shall be liable for the entire transport; where the loss occurs in a specific section of transport, the carrier that concludes the contract with the consignor and the carrier for that section shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 835 Where the goods are lost due to force majeure during the course of transport and the freight has not been collected, the carrier shall not be entitled to request payment of the freight; where the freight has already been collected, the consignor may request its return. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 836 Where the consignor or the consignee fails to pay the freight, storage fees, or other expenses, the carrier shall have a lien on the corresponding transported goods, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.
Article 837 Where the consignee is unknown or the consignee refuses to take delivery of the goods without just cause, the carrier may deposit the goods in accordance with the law.

Article 838 The multimodal transport operator shall be responsible for performing or organizing the performance of the multimodal transport contract, and shall enjoy the rights and assume the obligations of a carrier for the entire carriage.

Article 839 The multimodal transport operator may agree with the carriers of the various sections participating in the multimodal transport on their respective responsibilities for the carriage in each section under the multimodal transport contract; however, such agreement shall not affect the obligations of the multimodal transport operator for the entire carriage.

Article 840 Upon receiving the goods delivered by the consignor, the multimodal transport operator shall issue a multimodal transport document. At the request of the consignor, the multimodal transport document may be a negotiable document or a non-negotiable document.

Article 841 Where losses are caused to the multimodal transport operator due to the fault of the consignor when consigning the goods, the consignor shall still bear the liability for compensation even if the consignor has already transferred the multimodal transport document.

Article 842 Where the damage to or loss of goods occurs during a certain transport section of the multimodal transport, the multimodal transport operator's liability for compensation and the limitation of liability shall be governed by the provisions of the relevant laws that regulate the mode of transport of that section; where the transport section in which such damage or loss occurs cannot be determined, the liability for compensation shall be borne in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

Article 843 A technology contract is a contract concluded by the parties to establish their mutual rights and obligations in respect of technology development, transfer, licensing, consulting, or services.

Article 844 A technology contract shall be concluded in a manner conducive to the protection of intellectual property and the advancement of science and technology, and to the promotion of the research and development, transformation, application, and dissemination of scientific and technological achievements.

Article 845 The contents of a technology contract generally include clauses such as the name of the project, the subject matter, content, scope, and requirements, the plan, place, and method of performance, the confidentiality of technical information and materials, the ownership of technological achievements and the method of distribution of proceeds, the acceptance criteria and methods, and the explanation of terms and terminology.
Technical background materials, feasibility studies and technical evaluation reports, project task statements and plans, technical standards, technical specifications, original designs and process documents, and other technical documentation related to the performance of the contract may, as agreed by the parties, constitute a part of the contract.
Where a technology contract involves a patent, it shall indicate the name of the invention or creation, the patent applicant and patent holder, the date of application, the application number, the patent number, and the term of validity of the patent right.

Article 846 The method of payment of the price, remuneration, or royalties under a technology contract shall be agreed upon by the parties, and may be made by way of a lump sum payment, a lump sum payment in installments, a royalty payment, or a royalty payment with an initial upfront fee.
Where a royalty payment is agreed upon, it may be calculated as a certain percentage of the product price, or the increase in output value, profit, or product sales volume generated after the implementation of the patent or use of the technical know-how, or as otherwise agreed. The royalty percentage may be a fixed percentage, a progressively increasing percentage, or a progressively decreasing percentage.
Where a royalty payment is agreed upon, the parties may agree on a method for inspecting the relevant accounting books.

Article 847 Where the right to use and the right to transfer a job-related technological achievement vest in a legal person or an unincorporated organization, such legal person or unincorporated organization may conclude a technology contract regarding such job-related technological achievement. When a legal person or an unincorporated organization concludes a technology contract to transfer a job-related technological achievement, the person who accomplished such job-related technological achievement shall have the right of first refusal under the same conditions.
A job-related technological achievement is a technological achievement accomplished in the performance of a task assigned by a legal person or an unincorporated organization, or mainly by using the material and technical resources of such legal person or unincorporated organization.

Article 848 The right to use and the right to transfer a non-job-related technological achievement vest in the individual who accomplished such technological achievement, and such individual may conclude a technology contract regarding such non-job-related technological achievement.

Article 849 An individual who accomplishes a technological achievement shall have the right to be named as the person who accomplished it in the relevant technological achievement documents, and the right to obtain honorary certificates and awards.
Article 850 A technology contract that illegally monopolizes technology or infringes upon another person's technological achievements shall be void.

Article 851 A technology development contract is a contract concluded between the parties for the research and development of new technologies, new products, new processes, new varieties, or new materials, and their systems.
Technology development contracts include commissioned development contracts and collaborative development contracts.
A technology development contract shall be in written form.
A contract concluded between the parties for the purpose of implementing the transformation of scientific and technological achievements of practical value shall be governed by reference to the relevant provisions on technology development contracts.

Article 852 The commissioning party under a commissioned development contract shall, as agreed, pay the research and development funding and remuneration, provide technical materials, specify research and development requirements, complete collaborative matters, and accept the research and development results.

Article 853 The research and developer under a commissioned development contract shall, as agreed, formulate and implement a research and development plan, use the research and development funds reasonably, complete the research and development work on time, deliver the research and development results, provide relevant technical materials and necessary technical guidance, and assist the commissioning party in mastering the research and development results.

Article 854 Where a party to a commissioned development contract violates the agreement, causing the research and development work to be halted, delayed, or unsuccessful, it shall bear liability for breach of contract.

Article 855 The parties to a collaborative development contract shall, as agreed, make investments, including investments in the form of technology, divide the work to participate in the research and development, and collaborate and cooperate in the research and development work.

Article 856 Where a party to a collaborative development contract violates the agreement, causing the research and development work to be halted, delayed, or unsuccessful, it shall bear liability for breach of contract.

Article 857 Where the technology that is the subject matter of a technology development contract has been disclosed by another party, rendering the performance of the contract meaningless, the parties may rescind the contract.

Article 858 Where, during the performance of a technology development contract, the research and development fails or partially fails due to insurmountable technical difficulties, the risk shall be borne as agreed by the parties; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined pursuant to Article 510 of this Law, the risk shall be reasonably apportioned among the parties.
Where one party discovers a circumstance as specified in the preceding paragraph that may cause the research and development to fail or partially fail, it shall promptly notify the other party and take appropriate measures to reduce the loss; if it fails to promptly notify and take appropriate measures, causing the loss to expand, it shall bear liability for the expanded loss.

Article 859 Unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties, the right to apply for a patent for an invention or creation accomplished through commissioned development shall belong to the research and developer. Where the research and developer obtains the patent right, the commissioning party may exploit the patent in accordance with the law.
Where the research and developer transfers the right to apply for a patent, the commissioning party shall have the right of first refusal under the same conditions.

Article 860 The right to apply for a patent for an invention or creation accomplished through collaborative development shall be jointly owned by the parties to the collaborative development; where one party transfers its share of the joint right to apply for a patent, the other parties shall have the right of first refusal under the same conditions, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
Where one party to the collaborative development renounces its share of the joint right to apply for a patent, the other party or parties may file the application separately or jointly, unless otherwise agreed by the parties. Where the applicant obtains the patent right, the party that renounced the right to apply for the patent may exploit the patent free of charge.
Where one party to the collaborative development does not agree to file a patent application, the other party or parties may not file the patent application.

Article 861: The right to use, the right to transfer, and the method for distributing the benefits of technical secret achievements developed through commissioned development or cooperative development shall be agreed upon by the parties. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it still cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, each party shall have the right to use and transfer the achievements before the same technical solution is granted a patent right. However, the developer in commissioned development may not transfer the research and development achievements to a third party before delivering them to the commissioning party.

Article 862: A technology transfer contract is a contract under which the right holder lawfully owning the technology assigns to another party the relevant rights to an existing specific patent, patent application, or technical secret. A technology license contract is a contract under which the right holder lawfully owning the technology licenses another party to exploit or use the relevant rights to an existing specific patent or technical secret. The stipulations in a technology transfer contract or a technology license contract concerning the provision of specialized equipment or raw materials for exploiting the technology, or the provision of relevant technical consultation or technical services, shall be part of the contract.

Article 863: Technology transfer contracts include contracts for the transfer of patent rights, the transfer of patent application rights, and the transfer of technical secrets. Technology license contracts include contracts for patent exploitation licenses and technical secret use licenses. Technology transfer contracts and technology license contracts shall be made in writing.

Article 864: Technology transfer contracts and technology license contracts may specify the scope of exploiting the patent or using the technical secret, but they shall not restrict technological competition or technological development.

Article 865: A patent exploitation license contract shall be valid only within the duration of the patent right. If the term of validity of the patent right expires or the patent right is declared invalid, the patentee may not enter into a patent exploitation license contract with another party regarding that patent.

Article 866: The licensor under a patent exploitation license contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, license the licensee to exploit the patent, deliver the technical materials related to the exploitation of the patent, and provide necessary technical guidance.

Article 867: The licensee under a patent exploitation license contract shall exploit the patent in accordance with the agreement, shall not license a third party other than those agreed upon to exploit the patent, and shall pay the royalties as agreed.

Article 868: The transferor under a technical secret transfer contract and the licensor under a technical secret use license contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, provide technical materials, provide technical guidance, ensure the practicality and reliability of the technology, and assume the obligation of confidentiality. The confidentiality obligation specified in the preceding paragraph shall not restrict the licensor from applying for a patent, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 869: The transferee under a technical secret transfer contract and the licensee under a technical secret use license contract shall use the technology in accordance with the agreement, pay the transfer fee or royalties, and assume the obligation of confidentiality.

Article 870: The transferor under a technology transfer contract and the licensor under a technology license contract shall guarantee that they are the lawful owner of the technology provided and that the technology provided is complete, error-free, effective, and capable of achieving the agreed objectives.

Article 871: The transferee under a technology transfer contract and the licensee under a technology license contract shall, within the agreed scope and period, assume the obligation of confidentiality with respect to the undisclosed secret part of the technology provided by the transferor or licensor.

Article 872: If the licensor fails to license the technology in accordance with the agreement, it shall refund part or all of the royalties and shall bear liability for breach of contract. If the licensor exploits the patent or uses the technical secret beyond the agreed scope, or, in violation of the agreement, licenses a third party to exploit the patent or use the technical secret without authorization, it shall cease the breach and bear liability for breach of contract. If the licensor violates the agreed confidentiality obligation, it shall bear liability for breach of contract. The liability for breach of contract of the transferor shall be determined with reference to the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 873: If the licensee fails to pay the royalties in accordance with the agreement, it shall pay the arrears of royalties and pay liquidated damages as agreed; if it fails to pay the arrears of royalties or liquidated damages, it shall cease exploiting the patent or using the technical secret, return the technical materials, and bear liability for breach of contract. If the licensee exploits the patent or uses the technical secret beyond the agreed scope, or, without the licensor's consent, licenses a third party to exploit the patent or use the technical secret without authorization, it shall cease the breach and bear liability for breach of contract. If the licensee violates the agreed confidentiality obligation, it shall bear liability for breach of contract. The liability for breach of contract of the transferee shall be determined with reference to the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 874: If the transferee or licensee infringes upon another person's lawful rights and interests by exploiting the patent or using the technical secret in accordance with the agreement, the transferor or licensor shall bear the liability, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 875: The parties may, in accordance with the principle of mutual benefit, agree in the contract on the method for sharing the technical achievements arising from the subsequent improvement of the exploited patent or the used technical secret. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it still cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the other parties shall have no right to share the technical achievements subsequently improved by one party.

Article 876: The transfer and licensing of other intellectual property rights, such as the exclusive right of layout design of integrated circuits, the right of new plant varieties, and the copyright of computer software, shall be subject to the relevant provisions of this Section by reference.
Article 877: Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise on technology import and export contracts or contracts for patents or patent applications, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 878: A technical consultation contract is a contract under which one party, using its technical knowledge, provides the other party with feasibility studies, technical forecasts, special technical investigations, analysis and evaluation reports, and the like, for a specific technical project. A technical service contract is a contract under which one party, using its technical knowledge, solves a specific technical problem for the other party, excluding a work contract and a construction project contract.

Article 879: The client under a technical consultation contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, clarify the issues for consultation, provide technical background materials and relevant technical data, accept the work results of the受托人, and pay the remuneration.

Article 880: The受托人 under a technical consultation contract shall complete the consultation report or answer questions within the agreed period, and the consultation report submitted shall meet the agreed requirements.

Article 881 Where the client under a technical consulting contract fails to provide necessary information as agreed, thereby affecting the progress and quality of the work, or does not accept or accepts the work results later than the agreed time, the remuneration already paid shall not be recovered, and the unpaid remuneration shall be paid.
Where the受托人 under a technical consulting contract fails to submit the consulting report on time or the submitted consulting report does not comply with the agreement, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract such as reducing or exempting the remuneration.
The losses incurred from the decision made by the client under a technical consulting contract in accordance with the consulting report and opinions that meet the agreed requirements of the受托人 shall be borne by the client, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
Article 882 The client under a technical service contract shall provide working conditions as agreed, complete the matters of cooperation, accept the work results, and pay the remuneration.

Article 883 The受托人 under a technical service contract shall complete the service items as agreed, solve technical problems, guarantee the quality of work, and impart the knowledge for solving technical problems.

Article 884 Where the client under a technical service contract fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner not conforming to the agreement, thereby affecting the progress and quality of the work, or does not accept or accepts the work results later than the agreed time, the remuneration already paid shall not be recovered, and the unpaid remuneration shall be paid.
Where the受托人 under a technical service contract fails to complete the service work as agreed, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract such as exemption from remuneration.

Article 885 During the performance of a technical consulting contract or a technical service contract, new technological achievements made by the受托人 using the technical materials and working conditions provided by the client shall belong to the受托人. New technological achievements made by the client using the work results of the受托人 shall belong to the client. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 886 Where a technical consulting contract or a technical service contract has no agreement or unclear agreement on the burden of expenses necessary for the受托人 to carry out its work normally, such expenses shall be borne by the受托人.
Article 887 Where laws or administrative regulations have otherwise provided for technology intermediary contracts or technology training contracts, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 888 A deposit contract is a contract under which the depositary keeps the deposited item delivered by the depositor and returns such item.
Where a depositor engages in activities such as shopping, dining, or accommodation at the depositary's premises and deposits items at a designated place, it shall be deemed as a deposit, unless the parties have otherwise agreed or there is a different trade practice.

Article 889 The depositor shall pay the deposit fee to the depositary as agreed.
Where the parties have no agreement or unclear agreement on the deposit fee, and it still cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, it shall be deemed as a gratuitous deposit.
Article 890 A deposit contract shall be formed upon the delivery of the deposited item, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.
Article 891 Where the depositor delivers the deposited item to the depositary, the depositary shall issue a deposit voucher, unless there is a different trade practice.

Article 892 The depositary shall properly keep the deposited item.
The parties may agree on the place or method of deposit. Unless in an emergency or to protect the interests of the depositor, the depositary shall not change the place or method of deposit without authorization.

Article 893 Where the deposited item delivered by the depositor has defects or requires special storage measures due to its nature, the depositor shall inform the depositary of the relevant circumstances. If the depositor fails to inform, causing loss to the deposited item, the depositary shall not be liable for compensation; if the depositary suffers loss as a result, the depositor shall be liable for compensation, unless the depositary knew or should have known and failed to take remedial measures.

Article 894 The depositary shall not transfer the deposited item to a third party for custody, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.
Where the depositary, in violation of the preceding paragraph, transfers the deposited item to a third party for custody, causing loss to the deposited item, it shall be liable for compensation.
Article 895 The depositary shall not use the deposited item or permit a third party to use it, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.

Article 896 Where a third party claims rights over the deposited item, the depositary shall perform the obligation to return the deposited item to the depositor, except where preservation or enforcement measures are taken against the deposited item in accordance with law.
Where a third party initiates a lawsuit against the depositary or applies for seizure of the deposited item, the depositary shall promptly notify the depositor.

Article 897 During the deposit period, if the deposited item is damaged or lost due to the depositary's failure to keep it properly, the depositary shall be liable for compensation. However, if the gratuitous depositary proves that it has no intention or gross negligence, it shall not be liable for compensation.

Article 898 Where the depositor deposits currency, negotiable securities, or other valuable items, it shall declare them to the depositary, and the depositary shall inspect or seal them; if the depositor fails to declare, after such items are damaged or lost, the depositary may compensate according to the standard for ordinary items.

Article 899 The depositor may retrieve the deposited item at any time.
Where the parties have no agreement or unclear agreement on the deposit period, the depositary may request the depositor to retrieve the deposited item at any time; if the deposit period is agreed upon, the depositary shall not request the depositor to retrieve the deposited item before the expiry of the period, unless there is a special reason.
Article 900 Upon the expiry of the deposit period or when the depositor retrieves the deposited item in advance, the depositary shall return the original item and its fruits to the depositor.

Article 901 If a depositary keeps currency, it may return the same type and quantity of currency; if it keeps other fungible items, it may return items of the same type, quality, and quantity in accordance with the agreement.

Article 902 For a remunerated deposit contract, the depositor shall pay the deposit fee to the depositary within the agreed term.
If the parties have not agreed on the payment term or the agreement is unclear and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the fee shall be paid at the same time as the deposited item is collected.
Article 903 If the depositor fails to pay the deposit fee or other expenses as agreed, the depositary has a lien over the deposited item, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.
Article 904 A warehousing contract is a contract under which the depositary stores the goods delivered by the depositor for storage, and the depositor pays the warehousing fee.
Article 905 A warehousing contract is concluded upon the mutual agreement of the depositary and the depositor.

Article 906 If materials that are flammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, radioactive, or otherwise dangerous, or that are perishable, are stored, the depositor shall explain the nature of such materials and provide relevant information.
If the depositor violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the depositary may refuse to accept the deposited goods, or may take corresponding measures to avoid the occurrence of losses, and the expenses incurred thereby shall be borne by the depositor.
If the depositary stores materials that are flammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, radioactive, or otherwise dangerous, it shall have the corresponding storage conditions.

Article 907 The depositary shall inspect the goods upon their entry into the warehouse in accordance with the agreement. If the depositary discovers during inspection that the goods deposited do not conform to the agreement, it shall promptly notify the depositor. After inspection by the depositary, if the type, quantity, or quality of the stored goods do not conform to the agreement, the depositary shall bear compensation liability.
Article 908 When the depositor delivers the stored goods, the depositary shall issue certificates such as a warehouse receipt or entry note.

Article 910 A warehouse receipt is the document for taking delivery of the stored goods. If the depositor or holder of the warehouse receipt endorses the receipt and the depositary signs or affixes its seal, the right to take delivery of the stored goods may be transferred.
Article 911 Upon request of the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt, the depositary shall consent to their inspection of the stored goods or taking of samples.
Article 912 If the depositary discovers deterioration or other damage to the stored goods upon entry into the warehouse, it shall promptly notify the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt.

Article 913 If the depositary discovers deterioration or other damage to the stored goods upon entry into the warehouse that endangers the safety and proper storage of other goods, it shall urge the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt to take necessary measures. In an emergency, the depositary may take necessary measures; however, it shall promptly notify the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt of such situation afterwards.

Article 914 If the parties have not agreed on the storage period or the agreement is unclear, the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt may take delivery of the stored goods at any time, and the depositary may also request the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt to take delivery of the stored goods at any time, provided that a reasonable preparation period shall be given.

Article 915 Upon expiration of the storage period, the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt shall take delivery of the stored goods by presenting the warehouse receipt, entry note, or other certificates. If the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt takes delivery beyond the time limit, an additional warehousing fee shall be charged; if delivery is taken before the expiration of the period, the warehousing fee shall not be reduced.

Article 916 If the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt fails to take delivery of the stored goods upon expiration of the storage period, the depositary may urge them to take delivery within a reasonable period; if delivery is not taken after the expiration of such period, the depositary may deposit the stored goods with competent authorities.

Article 917 If stored goods are damaged or lost during the storage period due to improper storage by the depositary, the depositary shall bear compensation liability. If deterioration or damage of the stored goods is caused by the natural properties of the goods themselves, improper packaging not conforming to the agreement, or exceeding the effective storage period, the depositary shall not bear compensation liability.
Article 918 Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions on deposit contracts.
Article 919 A commission contract is a contract under which the principal and the agent agree that the agent shall handle the affairs of the principal.
Article 920 A principal may specifically authorize the agent to handle one or several matters, or may generally authorize the agent to handle all matters.

Article 921 The principal shall prepay the expenses for handling the entrusted matter. For the necessary expenses advanced by the agent in handling the entrusted matter, the principal shall reimburse such expenses and pay interest thereon.

Article 922 The agent shall handle the entrusted matter in accordance with the principal's instructions. If a change to the principal's instructions is necessary, the consent of the principal shall be obtained. Where it is difficult to contact the principal due to an emergency, the agent shall properly handle the entrusted matter; provided, however, that the agent shall, after the event, promptly report the situation to the principal.

Article 923 The agent shall handle the entrusted matter personally. With the consent of the principal, the agent may sub-entrust the matter. Where the sub-entrustment is consented to or ratified, the principal may give instructions directly to the third party on the entrusted matter, and the agent shall be liable only for the selection of the third party and for the instructions given to the third party. Where the sub-entrustment is not consented to or ratified, the agent shall be liable for the acts of the third party; except that, in an emergency, the agent needs to sub-entrust the matter to a third party in order to protect the interests of the principal.

Article 924 The agent shall, at the request of the principal, report on the progress of the entrusted matter. Upon termination of the agency mandate contract, the agent shall report on the outcome of the entrusted matter.

Article 925 Where the agent enters into a contract with a third party in its own name but within the scope of authority granted by the principal, and the third party knew at the time of entering into the contract of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, such contract shall directly bind the principal and the third party; except where there is definite evidence proving that the contract binds only the agent and the third party.

Article 926 Where, when the agent enters into a contract with a third party in its own name, the third party is unaware of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, and the agent fails to perform its obligation to the principal due to reasons attributable to the third party, the agent shall disclose the third party to the principal, whereupon the principal may exercise the rights of the agent against the third party. However, this shall not apply if the third party would not have entered into the contract had it known the identity of the principal when contracting with the agent.

Where the agent fails to perform its obligation to the third party due to reasons attributable to the principal, the agent shall disclose the principal to the third party, whereupon the third party may elect to assert its rights against either the agent or the principal as the counterparty; provided that the third party shall not change its elected counterparty.

Where the principal exercises the rights of the agent against the third party, the third party may assert against the principal any defenses it has against the agent. Where the third party elects the principal as its counterparty, the principal may assert against the third party any defenses it has against the agent, as well as any defenses the agent has against the third party.
Article 927 The property acquired by the agent in the course of handling the entrusted matter shall be delivered to the principal.

Article 928 If the agent completes the entrusted matter, the principal shall pay the agent remuneration as agreed.

Where the agency mandate contract is dissolved or the entrusted matter cannot be completed due to reasons not attributable to the agent, the principal shall pay the agent corresponding remuneration. Where the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 929 For a remunerated agency mandate contract, if the agent causes loss to the principal through its fault, the principal may claim compensation for the loss. For a non-remunerated agency mandate contract, if the agent causes loss to the principal through its intentional act or gross negligence, the principal may claim compensation for the loss.

Where the agent causes loss to the principal by acting beyond its authority, it shall compensate for the loss.
Article 930 If the agent suffers loss in the course of handling the entrusted matter due to reasons not attributable to itself, it may claim compensation for the loss from the principal.

Article 931 With the consent of the agent, the principal may entrust the entrusted matter to a third party in addition to the agent. If this causes loss to the agent, the agent may claim compensation for the loss from the principal.
Article 932 Where two or more agents jointly handle an entrusted matter, they shall bear joint and several liability to the principal.

Article 933 Either the principal or the agent may dissolve the agency mandate contract at any time. Where the dissolution of the contract causes loss to the other party, unless such loss is due to reasons not attributable to the dissolving party, the dissolving party under a non-remunerated agency mandate contract shall compensate for the direct loss caused by the improper timing of the dissolution, while the dissolving party under a remunerated agency mandate contract shall compensate for the other party's direct loss and the benefits that could have been obtained after performance of the contract.

Article 934 An agency mandate contract is terminated upon the death or cessation of existence of the principal, or upon the death, loss of civil capacity, or cessation of existence of the agent; except where the parties have otherwise agreed, or where it is inappropriate to terminate the contract given the nature of the entrusted matter.

Article 935 Where termination of an agency mandate contract due to the principal's death or being declared bankrupt or dissolved would harm the interests of the principal, the agent shall continue to handle the entrusted matter until the principal's successor, estate administrator, or liquidator assumes the entrusted matter.

Article 936 Where an agency mandate contract is terminated due to the agent's death, loss of civil capacity, or being declared bankrupt or dissolved, the agent's successor, estate administrator, legal representative, or liquidator shall promptly notify the principal. Where the termination of the contract would harm the interests of the principal, the agent's successor, estate administrator, legal representative, or liquidator shall take necessary measures before the principal undertakes subsequent arrangements.

Article 937 A property services contract is a contract whereby a property service provider provides property services, including the repair and maintenance of buildings and ancillary facilities, environmental hygiene, and management and maintenance of relevant order, within a property service area, and the owners pay property service fees.

Property service providers include property service enterprises and other managers.

Article 938 The content of a property services contract generally includes terms such as service items, service quality, standards and collection methods for service fees, use of maintenance funds, management and use of service premises, service period, and service handover.

Service commitments publicly made by a property service provider that are favorable to the owners shall be an integral part of the property services contract.

A property services contract shall be in writing.

Article 939 The preliminary property services contract concluded between a construction unit and a property service provider in accordance with law, and the property services contract concluded between the owners' committee and the property service provider elected by the owners' assembly in accordance with law, shall have legal binding force on the owners.

Article 940 Where, before the expiry of the service period stipulated in a preliminary property services contract concluded between a construction unit and a property service provider in accordance with law, a property services contract concluded between the owners' committee or the owners and a new property service provider becomes effective, the preliminary property services contract shall be terminated.

Article 941 Where a property service provider entrusts certain specialized service matters within the property service area to a professional service organization or another third party, it shall be liable to the owners for such specialized service matters.
A property service provider may not assign the entire property service it shall provide to a third party, or fragment the entire property service and assign it piecemeal to third parties.

Article 942 A property service provider shall, in accordance with the agreement and the nature of the property's use, properly repair, maintain, clean, landscape, and manage the common areas of the owners within the property service area, maintain basic order therein, and take reasonable measures to protect the safety of the owners' persons and property.
With respect to any act within the property service area that violates laws or regulations on public security, environmental protection, fire protection, or the like, the property service provider shall promptly take reasonable measures to stop it, report to the relevant administrative authority, and assist in handling it.

Article 943 A property service provider shall periodically disclose to the owners in a reasonable manner, and report to the owners' assembly and the owners' committee, the service items, responsible personnel, quality requirements, fee items, fee standards, performance status, as well as the use of maintenance funds, and the operation and income from the common areas of the owners.

Article 944 The owners shall pay property management fees to the property service provider as agreed. Where the property service provider has provided services in accordance with the agreement and relevant provisions, the owners may not refuse to pay the property management fees on the grounds that they have not accepted or do not need the relevant services.
If an owner fails to pay the property management fees within the agreed time limit in violation of the agreement, the property service provider may demand payment within a reasonable time limit by notice; if the owner still fails to pay upon expiry of the reasonable time limit, the property service provider may initiate legal proceedings or apply for arbitration.
A property service provider may not coerce payment of property management fees by suspending power supply, water supply, heat supply, gas supply, or the like.

Article 945 Where an owner decorates or renovates the premises, he shall inform the property service provider in advance, comply with the reasonable precautions pointed out by the property service provider, and cooperate with it in conducting necessary on-site inspections.
Where an owner transfers or leases the exclusive part of the property, creates a right of habitation, or changes the use of the common parts in accordance with law, he shall promptly inform the property service provider of the relevant circumstances.

Article 946 Where the owners jointly decide to dismiss the property service provider in accordance with the statutory procedures, they may dissolve the property service contract. Where they decide to dismiss, they shall notify the property service provider in writing sixty days in advance, unless the contract provides otherwise for the notice period.
