Where the dissolution of the contract pursuant to the preceding paragraph causes losses to the property service provider, the owners shall compensate for the losses, unless the cause for the dissolution is not attributable to the owners.

Article 947 Before the expiry of the property service term, if the owners jointly decide to re-engage the property service provider in accordance with law, they shall renew the property service contract with the original property service provider before the expiry of the contract term.
Before the expiry of the property service term, if the property service provider disagrees to being re-engaged, it shall notify the owners or the owners' committee in writing ninety days before the expiry of the contract term, unless the contract provides otherwise for the notice period.

Article 948 After the expiry of the property service term, if the owners fail to make a decision in accordance with law to re-engage the existing property service provider or to engage another one, and the property service provider continues to provide property services, the original property service contract remains valid, but the service term is indefinite.
Either party may dissolve an indefinite-term property service contract at any time, but shall notify the other party in writing sixty days in advance.

Article 949 Upon termination of a property service contract, the original property service provider shall withdraw from the property service area within the agreed or a reasonable time limit, return the property service premises, relevant facilities, and the relevant materials necessary for the property service to the owners' committee, the owners who have decided to self-manage, or the persons designated by them, cooperate with the new property service provider in the handover, and truthfully inform them of the condition of the property's use and management.
If the original property service provider violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, it may not request the owners to pay property management fees after the termination of the property service contract; if such violation causes losses to the owners, it shall compensate for the losses.

Article 950 After the termination of a property service contract, the original property service provider shall continue to handle property service matters until a new property service provider selected by the owners or the owners' assembly, or the owners who have decided to self-manage, takes over, and may request the owners to pay the property management fees for this period.
Article 951 A commission contract is a contract whereby a commission agent, in his own name, engages in trade activities for a principal, and the principal pays remuneration.
Article 952 The expenses incurred by the commission agent in handling the entrusted matter shall be borne by the commission agent, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Article 953 Where the commission agent is in possession of the subject matter, he shall keep it in good custody.

Article 954 If the subject matter delivered to the commission agent is defective or prone to decay or deterioration, the commission agent may dispose of it with the consent of the principal; if the commission agent is unable to contact the principal in a timely manner, he may dispose of it in a reasonable manner.

Article 955 Where a commission agent sells at a price lower than, or buys at a price higher than, that designated by the principal, he shall obtain the consent of the principal; if the sale or purchase takes place without the consent of the principal but the commission agent makes up the difference, the sale or purchase is binding on the principal.
Where a commission agent sells at a price higher than, or buys at a price lower than, that designated by the principal, he may claim additional remuneration as agreed; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined under Article 510 of this Law, the benefit belongs to the principal.
If the principal gives specific instructions on the price, the commission agent may not sell or buy in violation of such instructions.

Article 956 Where a commission agent sells or buys a commodity with a market price, unless the principal expresses an intention to the contrary, the commission agent may himself act as the buyer or seller.
Where the circumstances described in the preceding paragraph exist, the commission agent may still request the principal to pay remuneration.

Article 957 Where a commission agent buys the subject matter as agreed, the principal shall accept it in a timely manner. If, after being urged by the commission agent, the principal refuses to accept it without justifiable cause, the commission agent may deposit the subject matter in accordance with law.
If the subject matter cannot be sold or the principal withdraws the sale, and after being urged by the commission agent, the principal fails to retrieve or dispose of it, the commission agent may deposit the subject matter in accordance with law.

Article 958 Where a commission agent enters into a contract with a third party, the commission agent directly enjoys rights and assumes obligations under that contract.
If the third party's failure to perform its obligations causes damage to the principal, the commission agent shall be liable for compensation, unless otherwise agreed between the commission agent and the principal.

Article 959 Where a commission agent completes or partially completes the entrusted matter, the principal shall pay corresponding remuneration to him. If the principal fails to pay the remuneration within the time limit, the commission agent has a lien on the subject matter, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Article 960 Matters not covered in this Chapter shall be governed by reference to the relevant provisions on commission contracts.

Article 981 Where a manager manages another person's affairs, he/she shall adopt methods beneficial to the beneficiary. If interrupting the management is detrimental to the beneficiary, the management shall not be interrupted without justifiable reasons.

Article 982 Where a manager manages another person's affairs and is able to notify the beneficiary, he/she shall notify the beneficiary in a timely manner. If the managed affairs do not require urgent handling, the manager shall await the beneficiary's instructions.

Article 983 Upon conclusion of the management, the manager shall report to the beneficiary on the status of the managed affairs. Any property obtained by the manager from managing the affairs shall be promptly transferred to the beneficiary.

Article 984 Where the beneficiary subsequently ratifies the management of affairs by the manager, the relevant provisions on the entrustment contract shall apply from the beginning of the management of affairs, unless the manager expresses a contrary intention.

Article 986 Where a person enriched neither knew nor should have known that the benefits obtained lacked legal basis, and the benefits obtained no longer exist, such person shall not be obliged to return the benefits.

Article 987 Where a person enriched knew or should have known that the benefits obtained lacked legal basis, the aggrieved person may request the enriched person to return the benefits obtained and to compensate for losses according to law.

Article 988 Where a person enriched has already gratuitously transferred the obtained benefits to a third party, the aggrieved person may request the third party to assume the obligation to return the benefits within the corresponding scope.
Article 989 This Book governs civil relations arising from the enjoyment and protection of personality rights.

Article 990 Personality rights are the rights enjoyed by civil subjects, including the right to life, the right to personal integrity, the right to health, the right to name, the right to entity name, the right to portrait, the right to reputation, the right to honor, the right to privacy, and other rights.
In addition to the personality rights provided in the preceding paragraph, natural persons enjoy other personality rights and interests arising from personal freedom and personal dignity.
Article 991 The personality rights of civil subjects shall be protected by law, and no organization or individual may infringe upon them.
Article 992 Personality rights shall not be waived, transferred, or inherited.
Article 993 A civil subject may license others to use his/her name, entity name, portrait, etc., except where such licensing is prohibited by legal provisions or by the nature of the right.

Article 994 Where the name, portrait, reputation, honor, privacy, or remains of a deceased person are infringed upon, his/her spouse, children, and parents shall have the right to request in accordance with law that the tortfeasor bear civil liability; if the deceased has no spouse or children and the parents are deceased, other close relatives shall have the right to request in accordance with law that the tortfeasor bear civil liability.

Article 995 Where a personality right is infringed upon, the victim shall have the right to request in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other laws that the tortfeasor bear civil liability. The victim's claim for cessation of infringement, removal of obstruction, elimination of danger, elimination of adverse effects, restoration of reputation, and apology shall not be subject to the statute of limitations.

Article 996 Where a party's breach of contract damages the other party's personality rights and causes serious mental harm, the aggrieved party's choice to request the other party to bear liability for breach of contract shall not affect the aggrieved party's right to claim compensation for mental injury.

Article 997 Where a civil subject has evidence that a tortfeasor is committing or is about to commit an illegal act infringing upon his/her personality right, and failure to stop it promptly will cause irreparable damage to his/her lawful rights and interests, he/she shall have the right to apply to the People's Court in accordance with law for an order requiring the tortfeasor to cease the relevant acts.

Article 998 Factors such as the occupations of the tortfeasor and the victim, the scope of impact, the degree of fault, and the purpose, manner, and consequences of the act shall be considered in determining the tortfeasor's civil liability for infringing upon personality rights other than the right to life, personal integrity, and health.

Article 999 Where news reports or public opinion supervision are conducted for the public interest, the name, entity name, portrait, personal information, etc., of a civil subject may be reasonably used; if such use unreasonably infringes upon the personality rights of the civil subject, civil liability shall be borne in accordance with law.

Article 1000 Where a tortfeasor bears civil liability such as elimination of adverse effects, restoration of reputation, or apology for infringing upon personality rights, such liability shall be commensurate with the specific manner of the act and the scope of its impact.
Where a tortfeasor refuses to bear the civil liability provided in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court may enforce it by means such as publishing an announcement in newspapers or on the internet or publishing the effective judgment, and the expenses incurred thereby shall be borne by the tortfeasor.

Article 1001: The protection of identity rights arising from marital and family relations, among others, of a natural person shall be governed by the relevant provisions of Book One, Book Five, and other laws of this Code; where there are no such provisions, the relevant provisions on the protection of personality rights in this Book may be applied by reference based on the nature of such rights.

Article 1002: Natural persons enjoy the right to life. The safety and dignity of a natural person’s life shall be protected by law. No organization or individual may infringe upon another person’s right to life.

Article 1003: Natural persons enjoy the right to bodily integrity. The physical integrity and freedom of movement of a natural person shall be protected by law. No organization or individual may infringe upon another person’s right to bodily integrity.

Article 1004: Natural persons enjoy the right to health. The physical and mental health of a natural person shall be protected by law. No organization or individual may infringe upon another person’s right to health.

Article 1005: Where a natural person’s right to life, right to bodily integrity, or right to health is infringed upon or such person is in other dangerous situations, the organizations or individuals with a statutory duty to rescue shall provide timely assistance.

Article 1006: A person with full capacity for civil conduct shall have the right to independently decide, in accordance with the law, to donate their human cells, human tissues, human organs, or remains free of charge. No organization or individual may compel, deceive, or induce them into making such donation.
Where a person with full capacity for civil conduct consents to a donation in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it shall be made in writing, or a will may also be made.
If a natural person, during their lifetime, did not express an objection to donating, after such natural person’s death, their spouse, adult children, and parents may jointly decide on the donation, and the decision to donate shall be made in writing.

Article 1007: Any form of buying or selling human cells, human tissues, human organs, or remains is prohibited. Any act of buying or selling in violation of the preceding paragraph shall be null and void.

Article 1008: Where clinical trials are needed for the development of new drugs, medical devices, or the development of new prevention and treatment methods, the trials shall be approved by the relevant competent authorities in accordance with the law and reviewed and consented to by an ethics committee. The detailed information regarding the purpose, use, and potential risks of the trial, among others, shall be disclosed to the subject or the subject’s guardian, and written consent from them shall be obtained.
Where clinical trials are conducted, no trial fees may be charged to the subjects.

Article 1009: Medical and scientific research activities involving human genes, human embryos, or the like shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions, and shall not harm human health, violate ethical or moral principles, or harm the public interest.

Article 1010: Where a person commits sexual harassment against another person through words, text, images, physical acts, or otherwise, against the other person’s will, the victim shall have the right to request the actor to bear civil liability in accordance with the law. Organs, enterprises, schools, and other entities shall take reasonable measures such as prevention, acceptance of complaints, investigation, and handling to prevent and stop sexual harassment committed through the use of positions of power or subordinate relationships, among others.

Article 1011: Where a person deprives or restricts another person’s freedom of movement through illegal detention or other means, or illegally searches another person’s body, the victim shall have the right to request the actor to bear civil liability in accordance with the law.

Article 1012: Natural persons enjoy the right to a name, and have the right to decide, use, change, or permit others to use their own name in accordance with the law, provided that it does not violate public order or good customs.

Article 1013: Legal persons and unincorporated organizations enjoy the right to a name, and have the right to decide, use, change, assign, or permit others to use their own name in accordance with the law.
Article 1014: No organization or individual may infringe upon another person’s right to a name or right to an entity name by means of interference, misappropriation, counterfeiting, or otherwise.

Article 1015: A natural person shall adopt either the father’s surname or the mother’s surname, but may choose a surname different from either the father’s or the mother’s under any of the following circumstances:
(1) choosing the surname of another direct lineal elder relative by blood;
(2) being raised by someone other than the statutory supporter and choosing the supporter’s surname; or
(3) having other justifiable reasons that do not violate public order or good customs.
The surname of a natural person from an ethnic minority may follow the cultural traditions and customs of that ethnic group.

Article 1016: Where a natural person decides or changes their name, or a legal person or unincorporated organization decides, changes, or assigns its name, it shall go through the registration procedures with the relevant authority in accordance with the law, unless otherwise provided by law. Where a civil subject changes its name or entity name, the civil juristic acts performed before the change shall remain legally binding on it.

Article 1017: Pseudonyms, stage names, online names, translated names, trade names, and abbreviations of names and entity names that have a certain degree of social recognition and whose use by others is sufficient to cause public confusion shall be protected by reference to the relevant provisions on the protection of the right to a name and the right to an entity name.

Article 1018: Natural persons enjoy the right to a portrait, and have the right to create, use, disclose, or permit others to use their own portrait in accordance with the law. A portrait is the identifiable external image of a specific natural person reflected on a certain medium through images, sculptures, paintings, or other means.

Article 1019: No organization or individual may infringe upon another person’s right to a portrait by defacing, besmirching, or using information technology means to forge their portrait, among other means. Without the consent of the portrait right holder, the portrait of the portrait right holder may not be created, used, or disclosed, unless otherwise provided by law. Without the consent of the portrait right holder, the owner of a portrait work may not use or disclose the portrait of the portrait right holder by means such as publication, reproduction, distribution, rental, or exhibition.

Article 1021 Where a dispute arises between the parties regarding the understanding of the terms on the use of a portrait in a portrait licensing contract, an interpretation favorable to the portrait right holder shall be adopted.

Article 1022 Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the term of portrait licensing, either party may dissolve the portrait licensing contract at any time, provided that the other party shall be notified within a reasonable period in advance.
Where the parties have clearly agreed on the term of portrait licensing, and the portrait right holder has a legitimate reason, the portrait right holder may dissolve the portrait licensing contract, provided that the other party shall be notified within a reasonable period in advance. If the dissolution of the contract causes losses to the other party, compensation shall be paid for the losses, unless the cause is not attributable to the portrait right holder.

Article 1023 The licensing and use of names, among others, shall be governed by the relevant provisions on portrait licensing by reference.
The protection of the voice of a natural person shall be governed by the relevant provisions on the protection of the right to a portrait by reference.

Article 1024 Civil subjects shall enjoy the right to reputation. No organization or individual may infringe upon the right to reputation of another person by means of insult, defamation, or the like.
Reputation refers to the social evaluation of a civil subject in terms of moral character, prestige, talent, credit, and the like.

Article 1025 Where an actor, for the public interest, engages in news reporting, supervision by public opinion, or the like, which affects the reputation of another person, the actor shall not bear civil liability, except under any of the following circumstances:
(1) Fabricating or distorting facts;
(2) Failing to fulfill the duty of reasonable verification of seriously inaccurate content provided by another person; or
(3) Using insulting language or the like to derogate the reputation of another person.

Article 1027 Where literary or artistic works published by an actor describe real persons and real events or specific persons, contain insulting or defamatory content, and infringe upon the right to reputation of another person, the victim shall have the right to request in accordance with law that the actor bear civil liability.
Where literary or artistic works published by an actor do not describe a specific person, and merely the plot thereof is similar to the circumstances of that specific person, the actor shall not bear civil liability.

Article 1028 Where a civil subject has evidence proving that the content reported by media such as newspapers, periodicals, or the internet is inaccurate and infringes upon its right to reputation, it shall have the right to request the relevant media to promptly take necessary measures such as correction or deletion.

Article 1029 A civil subject may, in accordance with law, inquire into its own credit assessment; where it discovers that the credit assessment is improper, it shall have the right to raise an objection and request the adoption of necessary measures such as correction or deletion. The credit assessor shall promptly carry out verification, and if the credit assessment is found to be true upon verification, it shall promptly adopt necessary measures.

Article 1030 The relationship between a civil subject and a credit information processor such as a credit reference agency shall be governed by the provisions of this Book on the protection of personal information and the relevant provisions of other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 1031 Civil subjects shall enjoy the right to honor. No organization or individual may unlawfully deprive another person of his or her honorary titles, or slander or disparage the honor of another person.
Where an honorary title obtained should have been recorded but has not been recorded, the civil subject may request its recording; where there is an error in the recording of an honorary title obtained, the civil subject may request its correction.

Article 1032 Natural persons shall enjoy the right to privacy. No organization or individual may infringe upon the right to privacy of another person by such means as prying, intrusion, disclosure, or publication.
Privacy refers to the private life of a natural person that is peaceful and to the private spaces, private activities, and private information that he or she does not wish to be known to others.

Article 1034 The personal information of natural persons shall be protected by law.
Personal information refers to all kinds of information recorded electronically or by other means that can identify a specific natural person alone or in combination with other information, including the name, date of birth, identification number, biometric information, address, telephone number, email address, health information, whereabouts information, and the like, of a natural person.
Private information contained in personal information shall be governed by the provisions on the right to privacy; where there are no such provisions, the provisions on the protection of personal information shall apply.

Article 1036 An actor shall not bear civil liability for processing personal information under any of the following circumstances:
(1) The act is reasonably carried out within the scope of consent of the natural person or his or her guardian;
(2) The information that the natural person has made public himself or herself or other already lawfully disclosed information is reasonably processed, unless the natural person expressly refuses or the processing of such information infringes upon his or her material interests; or
(3) Other acts are reasonably carried out to safeguard the public interest or the lawful rights and interests of the natural person.

Article 1037 A natural person may, in accordance with law, inspect or copy his or her personal information from the information processor; where the natural person discovers an error in the information, he or she shall have the right to raise an objection and request the timely adoption of necessary measures such as correction.
Where a natural person discovers that an information processor processes his or her personal information in violation of the provisions of laws or administrative regulations or of the agreement between both parties, he or she shall have the right to request the information processor to promptly delete the information.

Article 1038 An information processor shall not disclose or falsify the personal information it has collected or stored; without the consent of the natural person, it shall not illegally provide such person's personal information to another person, except where the information has been processed and cannot be used to identify a specific person and cannot be restored.
An information processor shall adopt technical measures and other necessary measures to ensure the security of the personal information it has collected or stored and to prevent the information from being disclosed, falsified, or lost; where the disclosure, falsification, or loss of personal information occurs or is likely to occur, it shall promptly adopt remedial measures, notify the natural person in accordance with the relevant provisions, and report to the relevant competent authorities.

Article 1039 State organs, statutory bodies performing administrative functions, and their staff members shall keep confidential the privacy and personal information of natural persons that they become aware of in the course of performing their duties, and shall not disclose or illegally provide it to another person.
Article 1040 This Book regulates the civil relations arising from marriage and family relationships.

Article 1041 Marriage and family shall be protected by the State. A marriage system based on freedom of marriage, monogamy, and equality between men and women shall be implemented. The lawful rights and interests of women, minors, the elderly, and persons with disabilities shall be protected.

Article 142 Arranged marriages, mercenary marriages, and other acts of interference in the freedom of marriage shall be prohibited. The exaction of money or gifts by means of marriage shall be prohibited. Bigamy shall be prohibited. Any person who has a spouse shall be prohibited from cohabiting with another person. Domestic violence shall be prohibited. Abuse and desertion of family members shall be prohibited.

Article 1043 A family shall establish a fine family tradition, promote family virtues, and attach importance to the development of family civilization. Husband and wife shall be faithful to, respect, and care for each other. Family members shall respect the elders and love the young, help each other, and maintain a marriage and family relationship of equality, harmony, and civilization.

Article 1044 Adoption shall follow the principle of best interests of the adoptee and protect the lawful rights and interests of the adoptee and the adopter. The sale of minors in the name of adoption shall be prohibited.

Article 1045 Relatives include spouses, blood relatives, and in-laws. Spouses, parents, children, siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, paternal grandchildren, and maternal grandchildren shall be close relatives. Spouses, parents, children, and other close relatives living together shall be family members.

Article 1046 Marriage shall be based on the complete willingness of both the man and the woman. It shall be prohibited for either party to use compulsion over the other party, and no organization or individual may interfere with it.
Article 1047 The age of marriage shall not be earlier than 22 years of age for a male and 20 years of age for a female.
Article 1048 Marriage between lineal blood relatives or between collateral blood relatives within three generations shall be prohibited.

Article 1049 Both the man and the woman who intend to get married shall apply for marriage registration in person at the marriage registration authority. If the conditions set forth in this Law are satisfied, the marriage shall be registered and a marriage certificate shall be issued. Once marriage registration is completed, the marital relationship shall be established. Those who have not registered their marriage shall go through the registration procedures.
Article 1050 After marriage registration, upon agreement by both the man and the woman, the woman may become a member of the man's family, and the man may become a member of the woman's family.
Article 1051 A marriage shall be void under any of the following circumstances: (1) bigamy; (2) having a prohibited degree of kinship; (3) being under the lawful marriage age.

Article 1052 If a marriage is entered into under duress, the coerced party may request the People's Court to have the marriage annulled. A request to have the marriage annulled shall be made within one year from the date on which the coercive act ceases. If a party whose personal freedom has been unlawfully restrained requests to have the marriage annulled, the request shall be made within one year from the date on which his or her personal freedom is restored.

Article 1053 If one party suffers from a serious illness, the other party shall be truthfully informed before marriage registration. If such information is not truthfully provided, the other party may request the People's Court to have the marriage annulled. A request to have the marriage annulled shall be made within one year from the date on which the requesting party knows or should have known the grounds for annulment.

Article 1054 A void or annulled marriage shall have no legal effect from its inception, and the parties shall not have the rights or obligations of husband and wife. Property acquired during the period of cohabitation shall be disposed of by agreement between the parties; if an agreement cannot be reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment in accordance with the principle of favoring the faultless party. In the case of a void marriage caused by bigamy, the disposition of property shall not infringe upon the property rights and interests of the party to the lawful marriage. The children born of the parties shall be subject to the provisions of this Law concerning parents and children.Where a marriage is void or annulled, the faultless party has the right to claim damages.
Article 1055 Husband and wife shall enjoy equal status in the marriage and family.
Article 1056 Both the husband and the wife have the right to use their own surnames.
Article 1057 Both the husband and the wife have the freedom to engage in production, work, study, and social activities, and neither party may place restrictions on or interfere with the other party.
Article 1058 Both the husband and the wife shall equally enjoy the rights and jointly undertake the duties to raise, educate, and protect their minor children.

Article 1059 Husband and wife have the duty to support each other. If one party needs support and the other party fails to fulfill the obligation of support, the party in need has the right to claim alimony from the other party.

Article 1060 A civil juristic act performed by either spouse for the purpose of daily needs of the family shall be binding upon both spouses, unless the spouse and the other party have otherwise agreed. Any restriction imposed by the spouses on the scope of civil juristic acts that may be performed by one spouse shall not be a defense against a bona fide counterparty.
Article 1061 Husband and wife have the right to inherit each other’s estate.

Article 1064 Debts incurred by both spouses jointly signing a contract or by one spouse subsequently ratifying a contract with the other’s consent, as well as debts incurred by one spouse in his or her own name for the daily needs of the family during the existence of the marital relationship, shall be joint debts of the husband and wife.
If a debt is incurred by one spouse in his or her own name and exceeds the daily needs of the family during the existence of the marital relationship, it shall not be a joint debt of the husband and wife; unless the creditor is able to prove that the debt has been used for husband and wife’s common living or joint business operation, or that the debt was incurred based on the common manifestation of intent of both husband and wife.

Article 1065 Both parties, male and female, may agree that property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship and their premarital property shall be owned separately, owned jointly, or partly owned separately and partly owned jointly. Such an agreement shall be in writing. In the absence of such an agreement or where the agreement is ambiguous, the provisions of Articles 1062 and 1063 of this Code shall apply.
The agreement between husband and wife on property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship and premarital property shall be legally binding on both parties.
Where a husband and wife have agreed that property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship is owned separately, and the other party is aware of this agreement when a debt is incurred by one spouse in his or her own name with respect to the other party, the debt shall be satisfied with the separate property of that spouse.

Article 1066 During the existence of the marital relationship, if either of the following circumstances exists, a spouse may petition the People’s Court for partition of the community property:
(1) the other spouse has committed any act that seriously damages the interests of the community property, such as concealing, transferring, selling off, damaging, or squandering the community property, or forging community debts; or
(2) a person for whom one spouse has a statutory duty of support suffers from a serious illness requiring medical treatment, but the other spouse refuses to pay the relevant medical expenses.

Article 1067 Where parents fail to fulfill their duty of maintenance, a minor child or an adult child who is unable to live independently shall have the right to demand that the parents pay child support.
Where an adult child fails to fulfill his/her duty of support, an able-bodied or financially destitute parent shall have the right to demand that the adult child pay alimony.
Article 1068 Parents have the right and duty to educate and protect their minor children. Where a minor child causes damage to another person, the parents shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 1069 Children shall respect their parents’ marital rights and may not interfere with their parents’ divorce, remarriage, or post-marital life. The duty of children to support their parents shall not terminate due to changes in the parents’ marital relationship.
Article 1070 Parents and children have the right to inherit each other’s estate.

Article 1071 Children born out of wedlock shall enjoy the same rights as children born in wedlock, and no organization or individual may harm or discriminate against them.
The biological father or mother who does not directly raise the child born out of wedlock shall bear the child support for the minor child or the adult child who is unable to live independently.

Article 1072 Stepparents and stepchildren shall not maltreat or discriminate against each other.
The relations of rights and duties between a stepfather or stepmother and their stepchildren who are raised and educated by them shall be governed by the provisions of this Code relating to the relations between parents and children.

Article 1073 Where either parent disputes a parent-child relationship and has justifiable grounds, he or she may bring an action in the People’s Court to confirm or deny the parent-child relationship.
Where an adult child disputes a parent-child relationship and has justifiable grounds, he or she may bring an action in the People’s Court to confirm the parent-child relationship.

Article 1074 Paternal grandparents and maternal grandparents who are able to bear the burden shall have the duty to raise their minor grandchildren whose parents are deceased or are unable to raise them.
Grandchildren who are able to bear the burden shall have the duty to support their paternal grandparents or maternal grandparents whose children are deceased or are unable to support them.

Article 1075 Elder brothers and elder sisters who are able to bear the burden shall have the duty to maintain their minor younger siblings whose parents are deceased or are unable to raise them.
Younger siblings who are raised by their elder brothers or elder sisters and are able to bear the burden shall have the duty to maintain their elder brothers or elder sisters who lack the ability to work and have no source of income.

Article 1076 If husband and wife both desire to divorce voluntarily, they shall enter into a written divorce agreement and apply in person to the marriage registration authority for divorce registration.
The divorce agreement shall state the mutual desire of both parties to divorce voluntarily and the opinions agreed upon after negotiation on matters such as child support, property and debt disposal.

Article 1077 Within 30 days from the date the marriage registration authority receives the divorce application, if either party does not desire the divorce, he or she may withdraw the divorce application from the marriage registration authority.
Within 30 days after the expiry of the period provided in the preceding paragraph, both parties shall apply in person to the marriage registration authority for the issuance of a divorce certificate; if no such application is made, the divorce application shall be deemed to have been withdrawn.

Article 1078 After the marriage registration authority verifies that both parties do intend to divorce voluntarily and have reached consensus upon negotiation on matters such as child support, property and debt disposal, it shall register the divorce and issue a divorce certificate.
Article 1080 The marital relationship shall be dissolved upon the completion of divorce registration or upon the entry into effect of a divorce judgment or mediated settlement.
Article 1081: A spouse of a military personnel on active service requesting divorce shall obtain the consent of the military personnel, unless the military personnel has committed a major fault.

Article 1082: A husband may not file for divorce while the wife is pregnant, within one year after childbirth, or within six months after termination of pregnancy; however, this shall not apply if the wife files for divorce, or if the People's Court deems it necessary to accept the husband's divorce request.
Article 1083: After divorce, if both the man and woman voluntarily resume the marital relationship, they shall re-register the marriage at the marriage registration authority.

Article 1084: The parent-child relationship shall not be eliminated by parental divorce. After divorce, a child shall remain the child of both parents, regardless of whether the father or mother directly raises the child.
After divorce, parents shall retain the rights and obligations to raise, educate, and protect their children.
After divorce, a child under two years old shall be raised directly by the mother as a general rule. For a child who has reached the age of two, if the parents fail to reach an agreement on child-rearing issues, the People's Court shall make a judgment based on the specific circumstances of both parties, in accordance with the principle of what is most beneficial to the minor child. For a child who has reached the age of eight, their genuine wishes shall be respected.

Article 1085: After divorce, if one party directly raises the child, the other party shall bear part or all of the child support. The amount and duration of such payment shall be determined by agreement between the parties; if no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall make a judgment.
The agreement or judgment referred to in the preceding paragraph shall not prevent the child from making reasonable requests to either parent, when necessary, for an amount exceeding the original sum stipulated in the agreement or judgment.

Article 1086: After divorce, the parent who does not directly raise the child shall have the right to visit the child, and the other party has the obligation to cooperate.
The manner and timing of visitation rights shall be agreed upon by the parties; if no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall make a judgment.
If visitation by a father or mother is detrimental to the child's physical or mental health, the People's Court shall suspend visitation according to law; after the cause for suspension is eliminated, visitation shall be resumed.

Article 1087: Upon divorce, the common property of the husband and wife shall be disposed of by agreement between the parties; if no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall make a judgment based on the specific circumstances of the property, in accordance with the principle of giving consideration to the rights and interests of the child, the wife, and the innocent party.
Rights and interests of the husband or wife in family land contractual management, among others, shall be protected according to law.

Article 1088: If one spouse bears a greater share of obligations due to raising children, caring for the elderly, or assisting the other spouse's work, that spouse shall have the right to claim compensation from the other spouse upon divorce, and the other spouse shall provide such compensation. The specific method shall be agreed upon by the parties; if no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall make a judgment.

Article 1089: Upon divorce, the joint debts of the husband and wife shall be repaid jointly. If the common property is insufficient to pay off the debts, or if the property is separately owned by each party, the parties shall agree on the method of repayment; if no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall make a judgment.

Article 1090: Upon divorce, if one party has difficulty in living, the other party who is able to bear the cost shall provide appropriate assistance. The specific method shall be agreed upon by the parties; if no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall make a judgment.

Article 1092: If one spouse conceals, transfers, sells off, damages, or squanders common property, or forges joint debts to attempt to encroach upon the other spouse's property, the offending spouse may receive a smaller share or no share of the common property upon its division at divorce. After divorce, if the other spouse discovers any of the aforementioned acts, that spouse may file a lawsuit with the People's Court, requesting a re-division of the common property.
Article 1095: If both parents of a minor lack full civil capacity for conduct and may seriously endanger the minor, the guardian of the minor may place the minor out for adoption.

Article 1096: If a guardian places an orphan out for adoption, the guardian shall obtain the consent of the person obliged to maintain the orphan. If the person obliged to maintain the orphan does not consent to the placement for adoption, and the guardian is unwilling to continue fulfilling guardianship duties, a guardian shall be determined anew in accordance with the provisions of Book One of this Law.

Article 1097: If biological parents place their child out for adoption, they shall do so jointly. If one of the biological parents is unknown or cannot be found, the other parent may place the child out for adoption unilaterally.

Article 1099: Adoption of a child who is a collateral relative by blood of the same generation and within the third degree of kinship may be exempted from the restrictions provided in Article 1093, item (3), Article 1094, item (3), and Article 1102 of this Law.
An overseas Chinese who adopts a child who is a collateral relative by blood of the same generation and within the third degree of kinship may also be exempted from the restriction provided in Article 1098, item (1) of this Law.

Article 1100: An adoptive parent with no children may adopt up to two children; an adoptive parent with children may adopt only one child.
The adoption of an orphan, a minor with disabilities, or a minor raised by a children's welfare institution whose biological parents cannot be found shall not be subject to the restrictions of the preceding paragraph and Article 1098, item (1) of this Law.
Article 1101  If a person with a spouse intends to adopt a child, the husband and wife shall jointly make the adoption.
Article 1102  Where a person without a spouse adopts a child of the opposite sex, the age difference between the adopter and the adoptee shall be at least 40 years.

Article 1103  A step-father or step-mother may, with the consent of the biological parents of the step-child, adopt the step-child, and may be exempted from the restrictions provided for in Item (3) of Article 1093, Item (3) of Article 1094, Article 1098 and paragraph 1 of Article 1100 of this Law.

Article 1104  An adoption shall be based on the mutual willingness of both the adopter and the person placing out the child for adoption. Where a minor aged 8 or above is adopted, the adoptee's consent shall be obtained.

Article 1105  An adoption shall be registered with the civil affairs department of the people's government at or above the county level. The adoption relationship shall be established as of the date of registration.
Where a minor whose biological parents cannot be traced is adopted, the civil affairs department that handles the registration shall make a public announcement before the registration.
If the parties to the adoption relationship are willing to enter into an adoption agreement, they may do so.
If any or all of the parties to the adoption relationship request notarization of the adoption, notarization shall be carried out.
The civil affairs department of the people's government at or above the county level shall conduct an adoption assessment according to law.

Article 1106  After the establishment of an adoption relationship, the public security organ shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, complete the household registration for the adoptee.

Article 1107  Orphans or children whose biological parents are unable to raise them may be raised by relatives or friends of the biological parents. The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to the relationship between the caregiver and the child being cared for.
Article 1108  Where one spouse dies and the surviving spouse places their minor child out for adoption, the parents of the deceased spouse shall have the priority right to raise the child.

Article 1109  Aliens may, according to law, adopt children in the People's Republic of China.
An alien who adopts a child in the People's Republic of China shall obtain the consent for the adoption by examination from the competent authority of the country of which he or she is a national in accordance with the law of that country. The adopter shall provide supporting materials issued by an authorized institution of his or her country concerning his or her age, marital status, occupation, property, health, and whether he or she has a criminal record, etc., and shall sign a written agreement with the person placing out the child for adoption, and register in person with the civil affairs department of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
The supporting materials mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be authenticated by the foreign affairs authority of the adopter's country or an institution authorized by such authority, and also by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, unless the State provides otherwise.
Article 1110  Where the adopter or the person placing out the child for adoption requests that the adoption be kept confidential, others shall respect their wish and shall not disclose it.

Article 1111  From the date of establishment of the adoption relationship, the rights and obligations between the adoptive parents and the adopted child shall be governed by the provisions of this Law on the relationship between parents and children; the rights and obligations between the adopted child and the close relatives of the adoptive parents shall be governed by the provisions of this Law on the relationship between children and close relatives of the parents.
The rights and obligations between the adopted child and his or her biological parents and other close relatives shall be extinguished upon the establishment of the adoption relationship.

Article 1112  The adopted child may take the surname of the adoptive father or the adoptive mother, and may also retain his or her original surname upon agreement reached by the parties through consultation.

Article 1113  An adoption is void if it falls under the circumstances provided for in Book One of this Law concerning the invalidity of civil juristic acts or violates the provisions of this Book.
A void adoption shall have no legally binding force from the very beginning.

Article 1114  Before the adopted child reaches adulthood, the adopter shall not dissolve the adoption relationship, unless the adopter and the person placing out the child for adoption mutually agree to do so. If the adopted child is aged 8 or above, his or her consent shall be obtained.
If the adopter fails to perform the duty of raising the child and commits acts such as maltreatment or abandonment that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor adopted child, the person placing out the child for adoption shall have the right to request the dissolution of the adoption relationship between the adoptive parents and the adopted child. If the person placing out the child for adoption and the adopter fail to reach an agreement on the dissolution of the adoption relationship, they may file a lawsuit with the People's Court.

Article 1115  If the relationship between adoptive parents and an adult adopted child deteriorates to the extent that they cannot live together, the adoption relationship may be dissolved by agreement. If no agreement can be reached upon, they may file a lawsuit with the People's Court.

Article 1116  If the parties dissolve the adoption relationship by agreement, they shall go through the formalities of registering the dissolution of the adoption relationship with the civil affairs department.

Article 1117  After the adoption relationship is dissolved, the rights and obligations between the adopted child and the adoptive parents and their other close relatives shall be extinguished, and the rights and obligations between the adopted child and his or her biological parents and other close relatives shall be automatically restored. However, whether the adult adopted child's rights and obligations with his or her biological parents and other close relatives are restored may be determined through consultation.

Article 1118  After the dissolution of the adoption relationship, an adult adopted child who has been raised by the adoptive parents shall provide living expenses to the adoptive parents who lack the ability to work and have no source of income. If the adoption relationship is dissolved because the adult adopted child maltreated or abandoned the adoptive parents, the adoptive parents may demand compensation from the adopted child for the raising expenses incurred during the adoption period.
If the biological parents request the dissolution of the adoption relationship, the adoptive parents may demand appropriate compensation from the biological parents for the raising expenses incurred during the adoption period; however, this shall not apply if the adoption relationship is dissolved because the adoptive parents maltreated or abandoned the adopted child.
Article 1119  This Book governs the civil relations arising from succession.
Article 1120  The State protects the right of succession of natural persons.

Article 1121: Succession begins upon the death of the decedent.
Where several persons with a mutual succession relationship die in the same event and it is difficult to determine the time of death, the person with no other successor shall be presumed to have died first. Where all such persons have other successors, if they are of different generations, the senior generation shall be presumed to have died first; if they are of the same generation, they shall be presumed to have died simultaneously, and no succession shall occur between them.

Article 1122: Estate refers to the lawful personal property left by a natural person upon death.
Property that cannot be succeeded according to or by its nature shall not be succeeded.

Article 1123: Upon the commencement of succession, it shall be handled in accordance with statutory succession; if there is a will, it shall be handled in accordance with testamentary succession or legacy; if there is a legacy-support agreement, it shall be handled in accordance with the agreement.

Article 1124: Upon the commencement of succession, a successor who disclaims succession shall make a declaration in writing to disclaim succession before the disposition of the estate; failing such declaration, he or she shall be deemed to have accepted the succession.
A legatee shall, within sixty days after knowledge of the legacy, make a declaration of acceptance or disclaimer of the legacy; failing such declaration at the expiration of that period, he or she shall be deemed to have disclaimed the legacy.
Article 1126: The right of succession shall be equal between men and women.

Article 1127: The estate shall be succeeded in the following order:
(1) First order: spouse, children, parents;
(2) Second order: siblings, grandparents, maternal grandparents.
Upon the commencement of succession, the successors in the first order shall inherit, and those in the second order shall not inherit; if there is no first-order successor to inherit, the successors in the second order shall inherit.
The term "children" as used in this Book includes legitimate children, illegitimate children, adopted children, and stepchildren who have a relationship of support.
The term "parents" as used in this Book includes biological parents, adoptive parents, and stepparents who have a relationship of support.
The term "siblings" as used in this Book includes siblings of the same parents, half-siblings by blood, adopted siblings, and stepsiblings who have a relationship of support.

Article 1128: Where a child of the decedent predeceases the decedent, the lineal descendants of the deceased child shall take by representation.
Where a sibling of the decedent predeceases the decedent, the children of the deceased sibling shall take by representation.
A successor by representation may generally only succeed to the share of the estate that the person represented was entitled to succeed.

Article 1129: A widowed daughter-in-law who has fulfilled main maintenance obligations to her parents-in-law, or a widowed son-in-law who has fulfilled main maintenance obligations to his parents-in-law, shall be deemed a first-order successor.

Article 1130: The shares of the estate inherited by successors in the same order shall generally be equal.
Special care shall be given in the distribution of the estate to successors who have special financial difficulties or lack the ability to work.
In the distribution of the estate, successors who have fulfilled main maintenance obligations to the decedent or have lived with the decedent may receive a larger share.
Successors who have the ability and conditions to provide maintenance but fail to fulfill maintenance obligations shall receive no share or a smaller share in the distribution of the estate.
The shares may also be unequal if agreed upon by the successors through consultation.

Article 1131: An appropriate share of the estate may be given to a person, other than a successor, who was dependent on the maintenance of the decedent, or to a person, other than a successor, who provided more maintenance to the decedent.

Article 1132: Successors shall settle succession matters through consultation in the spirit of mutual understanding and forbearance, harmony and unity. The time, method, and shares of the division of the estate shall be determined by the successors through consultation; if consultation fails, the matter may be mediated by a People's Mediation Committee or a lawsuit may be instituted with the People's Court.

Article 1133: A natural person may, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, make a will to dispose of his or her personal property and may appoint an executor of the will.
A natural person may make a will to designate that his or her personal property be inherited by one or more of the statutory successors.
A natural person may make a will to donate his or her personal property to the state, a collective, or an organization or individual other than the statutory successors.
A natural person may, in accordance with the law, create a testamentary trust.
Article 1134: A holographic will shall be written by the testator in his or her own handwriting, signed, and dated with the year, month, and day.

Article 1135: A will written for another shall be witnessed by two or more witnesses, written by one of them on behalf of the testator, and signed by the testator, the writer, and the other witnesses, and dated with the year, month, and day.
Article 1136: A printed will shall be witnessed by two or more witnesses. The testator and the witnesses shall sign on each page of the will and date it with the year, month, and day.

Article 1137: A will made in the form of an audio or video recording shall be witnessed by two or more witnesses. The testator and the witnesses shall record their names or likenesses, as well as the year, month, and day, in the audio or video recording.

Article 1138: A testator may make a nuncupative will in an emergency situation. A nuncupative will shall be witnessed by two or more witnesses. Once the emergency situation is eliminated and the testator is able to make a will in writing or in the form of an audio or video recording, the nuncupative will so made shall be invalid.
Article 1139: A notarized will shall be made by the testator through a notary institution.
Article 1141 A will shall reserve the necessary share of the estate for an heir who lacks the ability to work and has no source of income.

Article 1142 A testator may revoke or alter his will.
Where, after making a will, the testator performs a civil juristic act that is contrary to the contents of the will, it is deemed a revocation of the relevant contents of the will.
Where there are several wills and their contents are contradictory, the last will shall prevail.

Article 1143 A will made by a person without civil capacity or with limited civil capacity is void.
A will must express the true intention of the testator. A will made under fraud or duress is void.
A forged will is void.
Where a will is tampered with, the tampered content is void.

Article 1144 Where testamentary succession or legacy is subject to an obligation, the heir or legatee shall perform the obligation. Where the obligation is not performed without justifiable cause, upon the request of an interested party or a relevant organization, the People's Court may revoke his right to receive the part of the estate subject to the obligation.

Article 1145 After the commencement of succession, the executor of the will shall serve as the estate administrator. If there is no executor of the will, the heirs shall promptly elect an estate administrator. If the heirs fail to elect, the heirs shall collectively serve as the estate administrator. If there is no heir or all heirs have renounced the succession, the civil affairs department or the villagers' committee at the place of the deceased's domicile before death shall serve as the estate administrator.
Article 1146 Where there is a dispute over the determination of the estate administrator, an interested party may apply to the People's Court for the appointment of an estate administrator.

Article 1148 The estate administrator shall perform his duties according to law. If he causes damage to the heirs, legatees, or creditors by intentional act or gross negligence, he shall bear civil liability.
Article 1149 The estate administrator may obtain remuneration in accordance with the provisions of the law or in accordance with an agreement.

Article 1150 After the commencement of succession, an heir who knows of the death of the deceased shall promptly notify the other heirs and the executor of the will. If none of the heirs knows of the death of the deceased or if the heir who knows of the death cannot do the notification, it shall be the responsibility of the unit to which the deceased belonged before his death or the residents' committee or villagers' committee at his domicile to notify them.
Article 1151 A person who is in possession of the estate shall take good care of it. No organization or individual may misappropriate it or scramble for it.

Article 1152 After the commencement of succession, if an heir dies before the estate is distributed and has not renounced the succession, the estate that such heir should inherit shall devolve upon his own heirs, except where otherwise provided for in the will.

Article 1153 In the case of community property of spouses, unless otherwise agreed, upon distribution of the estate, one-half of the community property shall be first allocated to the surviving spouse, and the remainder shall constitute the estate of the deceased.
Where the estate is part of the family property, the property of other persons shall be first severed before the estate is distributed.

Article 1155 Upon distribution of the estate, a share of the succession shall be preserved for a fetus. If the fetus is stillborn at delivery, the preserved share shall be dealt with in accordance with statutory succession.

Article 1156 The distribution of the estate shall be conducive to the needs of production and daily life and shall not impair the utility of the estate.
Where the estate is not suitable for division, it may be disposed of by way of valuation, appropriate compensation, or co-ownership.
Article 1157 Where the spouse of a deceased person remarries, he or she is entitled to dispose of the property inherited, and no organization or individual may interfere.

Article 1158 A natural person may enter into a legacy-support agreement with an organization or individual other than the heir. Under the agreement, the organization or individual shall assume the obligation to support the natural person in life, attend to his funeral and burial, and shall enjoy the right to the legacy.

Article 1159 Upon distributing the estate, the taxes and debts that the deceased should pay according to law shall be satisfied; however, necessary estate shall be reserved for an heir who lacks the ability to work and has no source of income.

Article 1160 An estate which is neither succeeded to nor legated to anyone shall belong to the State, and shall be used for public welfare undertakings. Where the deceased was a member of a collective-owned organization during his lifetime, the estate shall belong to the collective-owned organization to which he belonged.

Article 1161 An heir shall satisfy the taxes and debts that the decedent shall pay according to law within the actual value of the estate. An heir who voluntarily pays off the taxes and debts in excess of the actual value of the estate shall not be bound by this limitation.
Where an heir disclaims the inheritance, he or she may be relieved of the liability to satisfy the taxes and debts that the decedent shall pay according to law.
Article 1162 The execution of a legacy shall not prejudice the satisfaction of the taxes and debts that the testator shall pay according to law.

Article 1163 Where there is both statutory succession and testate succession or a legacy, the statutory heirs shall satisfy the taxes and debts that the decedent shall pay according to law; the portion exceeding the actual value of the estate under statutory succession shall be satisfied by the testamentary heirs and legatees in proportion to the estates they have received.
Article 1164 This Book regulates the civil relations arising from the infringement of civil rights and interests.

Article 1165 A person who through his or her fault infringes upon another person's civil rights and interests and causes damage shall bear tort liability.
Where a person is presumed to be at fault according to law and fails to prove that he or she is not at fault, he or she shall bear tort liability.

Article 1166 Where a person causes damage to another person's civil rights and interests regardless of whether he or she is at fault, and the law provides that he or she shall bear tort liability, such provisions shall apply.

Article 1167 Where a tortious act endangers another person's personal or property safety, the aggrieved person has the right to request the tortfeasor to bear the tort liabilities such as cessation of the infringement, removal of the obstruction, and elimination of the danger.
Article 1168 Where two or more persons jointly commit a tortious act causing damage to another person, they shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 1169 A person who instigates or assists another in committing a tortious act shall bear joint and several liability with the actor.
A person who instigates or assists a person without capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct in committing a tortious act shall bear tort liability; and the guardian of such person without capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct who fails to fulfill the duty of guardianship shall bear corresponding liability.

Article 1170 Where two or more persons commit acts endangering another person's personal or property safety, and the act of one or several of them causes damage to another person, if the specific tortfeasor can be identified, that tortfeasor shall bear liability; if the specific tortfeasor cannot be identified, all actors shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 1171 Where two or more persons respectively commit tortious acts causing the same damage, and each person's tortious act is sufficient to cause the entire damage, the actors shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 1172 Where two or more persons respectively commit tortious acts causing the same damage, and the extent of liability of each can be determined, they shall each bear corresponding liability; if the extent of liability is difficult to determine, they shall bear liability equally.
Article 1173 Where the aggrieved person is at fault for the occurrence or expansion of the same damage, the liability of the tortfeasor may be reduced.
Article 1174 Where the damage is caused intentionally by the victim, the actor shall not bear liability.
Article 1175 Where the damage is caused by a third party, the third party shall bear tort liability.

Article 1176 Where a person voluntarily participates in a cultural or sports activity with certain risks and sustains damage due to the conduct of another participant, the victim may not request such other participant to bear tort liability; unless the other participant has intentional or grossly negligent fault for the occurrence of the damage.
The liability of the organizer of the activity shall be governed by the provisions of Articles 1198 through 1201 of this Law.

Article 1177 Where a person's lawful rights and interests are infringed upon, and the situation is urgent and prompt protection by the State organs cannot be obtained, and failure to take immediate measures would cause irreparable damage to his or her lawful rights and interests, the victim may take reasonable measures, such as detaining the property of the tortfeasor, within the necessary scope of protecting his or her own lawful rights and interests; provided, however, that he or she shall immediately request the relevant State organs to handle the matter.
If the measures taken by the victim are improper and cause damage to another person, the victim shall bear tort liability.
Article 1178 Where this Law or other laws provide otherwise on the circumstances in which liability is not assumed or is reduced, such provisions shall apply.

Article 1179 Where a person tortiously causes personal injury to another person, compensation shall be made for the reasonable expenses incurred for treatment and rehabilitation, such as medical expenses, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, nutritional expenses, and hospital meal subsidies, as well as the income lost due to missed work. If disability is caused, compensation shall also be made for assistive device expenses and disability compensation; if death is caused, compensation shall also be made for funeral expenses and death compensation.
Article 1180 Where the same tortious act causes the death of multiple persons, an identical amount may be determined for death compensation.

Article 1181 Where an infringed person dies, his close relatives have the right to request the tortfeasor to assume tort liability. Where the infringed person is an organization and such organization is divided or merged, the organization that succeeds to the rights has the right to request the tortfeasor to assume tort liability.
Where an infringed person dies, a person who pays the reasonable expenses such as medical expenses and funeral expenses of the infringed person has the right to request the tortfeasor to compensate such expenses, unless the tortfeasor has already paid such expenses.

Article 1182 Where a tort infringes upon another person's personal rights and interests and causes property losses, the compensation shall be made according to the losses suffered by the infringed person or the benefits gained thereby by the tortfeasor. Where the losses suffered by the infringed person and the benefits gained by the tortfeasor are difficult to determine, and the infringed person and the tortfeasor fail to reach an agreement on the amount of compensation through consultation and file a lawsuit with the People's Court, the People's Court shall determine the amount of compensation based on the actual circumstances.

Article 1183 Where a tort infringes upon a natural person's personal rights and interests and causes serious mental harm, the infringed person has the right to claim compensation for mental harm.
Where a tort intentionally or with gross negligence infringes upon a natural person's specific item of personal significance and causes serious mental harm, the infringed person has the right to claim compensation for mental harm.
Article 1184 Where a tort infringes upon another person's property, the property losses shall be calculated according to the market price at the time the loss occurs or other reasonable methods.

Article 1185 Where a tort intentionally infringes upon another person's intellectual property rights and the circumstances are serious, the infringed person has the right to claim corresponding punitive damages.
Article 1186 Where neither the victim nor the actor is at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the loss shall be apportioned between the parties in accordance with the provisions of law.

Article 1187 After the damage occurs, the parties may negotiate the method of payment of the compensation. If they fail to reach an agreement through negotiation, the compensation shall be paid in a lump sum; if it is truly difficult to pay in a lump sum, it may be paid in installments, but the infringed person has the right to request the provision of corresponding security.

Article 1188 Where a person without legal capacity or a person with limited legal capacity causes damage to another person, the guardian shall assume the tort liability. If the guardian has fulfilled his guardianship duties, his tort liability may be mitigated.
Where a person without legal capacity or a person with limited legal capacity who has property causes damage to another person, the compensation shall be paid from his own property; for the insufficient part, the guardian shall compensate.

Article 1189 Where a person without legal capacity or a person with limited legal capacity causes damage to another person, and the guardian entrusts his guardianship duties to another person, the guardian shall assume the tort liability; if the trustee is at fault, he shall assume corresponding liability.

Article 1190 Where a person with full legal capacity, being temporarily unconscious or out of control of his conduct, causes damage to another person, if he is at fault, he shall assume tort liability; if he is not at fault, he shall make appropriate compensation to the victim based on his economic circumstances.
Where a person with full legal capacity causes damage to another person because he is temporarily unconscious or out of control of his conduct due to intoxication, or abuse of narcotic or psychotropic substances, he shall assume tort liability.

Article 1191 Where an employee of an employer causes damage to another person in the performance of his work tasks, the employer shall assume the tort liability. After the employer assumes tort liability, it may seek reimbursement from the employee who acted intentionally or with gross negligence.
During the period of labor dispatch, where a dispatched employee causes damage to another person in the performance of his work tasks, the accepting entity of the labor dispatch shall assume the tort liability; if the labor dispatch entity is at fault, it shall assume corresponding liability.

Article 1192 Where a labor relationship is formed between individuals, if the party providing labor causes damage to another person during the provision of labor, the party accepting labor shall assume the tort liability. After the party accepting labor assumes tort liability, it may seek reimbursement from the party providing labor who acted intentionally or with gross negligence. Where the party providing labor suffers damage during the provision of labor, the parties shall assume corresponding liability based on their respective fault.
During the period of providing labor, where damage is caused to the party providing labor by the act of a third party, the party providing labor has the right to request the third party to assume tort liability, and also has the right to request the party accepting labor to provide compensation. After the party accepting labor provides compensation, it may seek reimbursement from the third party.

Article 1193 Where a contractor, in the course of completing the work, causes damage to a third party or to himself, the client shall not assume tort liability. However, if the client is at fault for the commissioning, instructions, or selection, he shall assume corresponding liability.

Article 1194 Where a network user or network service provider infringes upon another person's civil rights and interests by using the network, it shall assume tort liability. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions prevail.

Article 1195 Where a network user commits a tortious act by using a network service, the right holder has the right to notify the network service provider to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, or disconnection of links. The notice shall include preliminary evidence of the infringement and the true identity information of the right holder.
After receiving the notice, the network service provider shall promptly forward such notice to the relevant network user and take necessary measures based on the preliminary evidence of the infringement and the type of service; if it fails to take necessary measures in a timely manner, it shall bear joint and several liability with the network user for the expanded part of the damage.
Where the right holder causes damage to a network user or network service provider due to an erroneous notice, it shall assume tort liability. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions prevail.

Article 1196 After receiving the forwarded notice, a network user may submit a declaration to the network service provider stating that no infringement exists. The declaration shall include preliminary evidence that no infringement exists and the true identity information of the network user.
After receiving the declaration, the network service provider shall forward such declaration to the right holder who issued the notice and inform the right holder that it may file a complaint with the relevant authority or initiate a lawsuit with the People's Court. If the network service provider does not receive notice from the right holder of having filed a complaint or initiated a lawsuit within a reasonable period after the forwarded declaration reaches the right holder, it shall promptly terminate the measures taken.

Article 1197 Where a network service provider knows or should know that a network user is using its network service to infringe upon another person's civil rights and interests, and fails to take necessary measures, it shall bear joint and several liability with such network user.

Article 1198 Where an operator or manager of business premises or public places such as hotels, shopping malls, banks, stations, airports, stadiums, or entertainment venues, or an organizer of mass activities fails to fulfill its security obligation and causes damage to another person, it shall assume tort liability.
Where damage is caused to another person by the act of a third party, the third party shall assume tort liability; if the operator, manager, or organizer fails to fulfill its security obligation, it shall assume corresponding supplementary liability. After the operator, manager, or organizer assumes supplementary liability, it may seek reimbursement from the third party.

Article 1199 Where a person without legal capacity suffers personal injury during the period of study or life in a kindergarten, school, or other educational institution, such kindergarten, school, or other educational institution shall assume tort liability; however, if it can prove that it has fulfilled its duties of education and management, it shall not assume tort liability.

Article 1200 Where a person with limited legal capacity suffers personal injury during the period of study or life in a school or other educational institution, and the school or other educational institution fails to fulfill its duties of education and management, it shall assume tort liability.
