Article 1201 Where a person who has no or limited capacity for civil conduct suffers personal injury during the period of study or life in a kindergarten, school, or other educational institution, caused by a third party other than the kindergarten, school, or other educational institution, the third party shall bear the tort liability; if the kindergarten, school, or other educational institution fails to fulfill its management duties, it shall bear the corresponding supplementary liability. The kindergarten, school, or other educational institution may, after bearing the supplementary liability, recover from the third party.
Article 1202 Where a person suffers harm due to a defect in a product, the manufacturer shall bear tort liability.

Article 1203 Where a person suffers harm due to a defect in a product, the injured party may claim compensation from the manufacturer of the product or from the seller of the product.
If the product defect was caused by the manufacturer, the seller, after paying compensation, is entitled to recover from the manufacturer. If the product defect was caused by the fault of the seller, the manufacturer, after paying compensation, is entitled to recover from the seller.

Article 1204 Where a product defect caused by the fault of a third party such as a carrier or warehouser results in harm to another person, the manufacturer or seller of the product, after paying compensation, is entitled to recover from the third party.

Article 1205 Where a product defect endangers the personal or property safety of another person, the injured party has the right to request the manufacturer or seller to bear tort liability such as cessation of the infringement, removal of the obstruction, or elimination of the danger.

Article 1206 Where a product is found to have a defect after being placed into circulation, the manufacturer or seller shall promptly take remedial measures such as cessation of sale, warning, or recall; if such remedial measures are not taken promptly or are inadequate, causing the harm to be expanded, the manufacturer or seller shall also bear tort liability for the expanded harm.
Where a recall measure is taken in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the manufacturer or seller shall bear the necessary expenses incurred by the injured party as a result.

Article 1207 Where a person knowingly manufactures or sells a product with a defect, or fails to take effective remedial measures in accordance with the provisions of the preceding article, thereby causing the death of another person or serious harm to the health of another person, the injured party has the right to request the corresponding punitive damages.

Article 1208 Where a motor vehicle is involved in a traffic accident causing harm, compensation liability shall be borne in accordance with the provisions of road traffic safety laws and the relevant provisions of this Law.

Article 1209 Where, under circumstances such as leasing or borrowing, the owner or manager of a motor vehicle is not the same person as the user, and a traffic accident occurs causing harm, if the liability is attributable to the motor vehicle side, the user of the motor vehicle shall bear compensation liability; if the owner or manager of the motor vehicle has fault in the occurrence of the harm, they shall bear the corresponding compensation liability.

Article 1210 Where the parties have transferred and delivered a motor vehicle through a sale or other means but have not processed the registration, and a traffic accident occurs causing harm, if the liability is attributable to the motor vehicle side, the transferee shall bear compensation liability.

Article 1211 Where a motor vehicle engaged in road transport business operations under a dependency arrangement causes harm in a traffic accident, and the liability is attributable to the motor vehicle side, the dependent party and the supporting party shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 1212 Where a person drives another person's motor vehicle without permission and a traffic accident occurs causing harm, if the liability is attributable to the motor vehicle side, the user of the motor vehicle shall bear compensation liability; if the owner or manager of the motor vehicle has fault in the occurrence of the harm, they shall bear the corresponding compensation liability, unless otherwise provided in this Chapter.

Article 1213 Where a motor vehicle is involved in a traffic accident causing harm, and the liability is attributable to the motor vehicle side, compensation shall first be made by the insurer providing compulsory motor vehicle insurance within the liability limit of the compulsory insurance; for the shortfall, compensation shall be made by the insurer providing commercial motor vehicle insurance in accordance with the insurance contract; if there is still a shortfall or if no commercial motor vehicle insurance is purchased, the tortfeasor shall pay compensation.

Article 1214 Where a motor vehicle that is assembled or has reached the scrap standard is transferred by sale or other means, and a traffic accident occurs causing harm, the transferor and the transferee shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 1215 Where a motor vehicle that has been stolen, robbed, or forcibly taken is involved in a traffic accident causing harm, the person who stole, robbed, or forcibly took the motor vehicle shall bear compensation liability. If the person who stole, robbed, or forcibly took the motor vehicle is not the same person as the user of the motor vehicle, and a traffic accident occurs causing harm attributable to the motor vehicle side, the person who stole, robbed, or forcibly took the motor vehicle and the user of the motor vehicle shall bear joint and several liability.
If the insurer advances rescue expenses within the liability limit of the compulsory motor vehicle insurance, it has the right to recover from the person liable for the traffic accident.

Article 1216 Where the driver of a motor vehicle flees after a traffic accident and the motor vehicle is covered by compulsory insurance, the insurer shall pay compensation within the liability limit of the compulsory motor vehicle insurance; if the motor vehicle is unknown, is not covered by compulsory insurance, or the rescue expenses exceed the liability limit of the compulsory motor vehicle insurance, and there is a need to pay for the rescue, funeral, and other expenses for the personal injury or death of the injured party, the road traffic accident social assistance fund shall advance such expenses. After the road traffic accident social assistance fund has made advances, its administrative authority has the right to recover from the person liable for the traffic accident.

Article 1217 Where a non-operating motor vehicle is involved in a traffic accident causing harm to a passenger being carried free of charge, and the liability is attributable to the motor vehicle side, the compensation liability shall be mitigated, unless the user of the motor vehicle acted intentionally or with gross negligence.

Article 1218 Where a patient suffers harm in the course of diagnosis and treatment activities and the medical institution or its medical staff is at fault, the medical institution shall bear compensation liability.

Article 1219 In the course of diagnosis and treatment activities, medical staff shall explain the patient's condition and medical measures to the patient. Where a surgical procedure, special examination, or special treatment is to be performed, medical staff shall promptly provide the patient with specific explanations concerning the medical risks, alternative treatment plans, and other relevant information, and obtain the patient's explicit consent; if it is impossible or inappropriate to explain to the patient, explanations shall be given to the patient's close relatives, and their explicit consent shall be obtained.
Where medical staff fail to fulfill the obligations set forth in the preceding paragraph, causing harm to the patient, the medical institution shall bear compensation liability.

Article 1220 In emergency situations such as rescuing a patient whose life is in critical danger, where the opinion of the patient or the patient's close relatives cannot be obtained, the corresponding medical measures may be immediately implemented with the approval of the person in charge of the medical institution or an authorized person in charge.

Article 1221 Where a medical worker fails to fulfill the duty of care corresponding to the prevailing medical standards in diagnosis and treatment activities, causing damage to a patient, the medical institution shall bear compensation liability.

Article 1222 Where a patient sustains damage in diagnosis and treatment activities, the medical institution shall be presumed at fault under any of the following circumstances:
(1) It violates any provision of laws, administrative regulations, rules, or other relevant diagnosis and treatment norms;
(2) It conceals or refuses to provide medical records related to the dispute; or
(3) It loses, forges, alters, or illegally destroys medical records.

Article 1223 Where a patient sustains damage due to defects in pharmaceutical products, disinfection products, or medical devices, or due to the transfusion of unqualified blood, the patient may claim compensation from the marketing authorization holder, the manufacturer, or the blood supply institution, and may also claim compensation from the medical institution. If the patient claims compensation from the medical institution, the medical institution, after paying compensation, shall have the right to seek recourse against the liable marketing authorization holder, manufacturer, or blood supply institution.

Article 1224 Where a patient sustains damage in diagnosis and treatment activities, the medical institution shall not bear compensation liability under any of the following circumstances:
(1) The patient or his close relatives fail to cooperate with the medical institution in diagnosis and treatment that complies with the diagnosis and treatment norms;
(2) The medical workers have fulfilled their reasonable duty of care in emergency situations such as rescuing a patient in critical condition; or
(3) The difficulty in diagnosis and treatment is attributable to the limitations of prevailing medical standards.
Where, under the circumstance specified in Item (1) of the preceding paragraph, the medical institution or its medical workers are also at fault, they shall bear corresponding compensation liability.

Article 1225 Medical institutions and their medical workers shall, in accordance with regulations, complete and properly keep medical records including hospitalization records, medical orders, test reports, surgical and anesthesia records, pathology data, and nursing records.
Where a patient requests to access or duplicate the medical records specified in the preceding paragraph, the medical institution shall provide them promptly.

Article 1226 Medical institutions and their medical workers shall maintain the confidentiality of patients' privacy and personal information. Anyone who divulges a patient's privacy or personal information, or discloses the patient's medical records without the patient's consent, shall bear tort liability.
Article 1227 Medical institutions and their medical workers shall not carry out unnecessary examinations in violation of diagnosis and treatment norms.

Article 1228 The legitimate rights and interests of medical institutions and their medical workers are protected by law.
Anyone who disrupts medical order, interferes with the work or life of medical workers, or infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of medical workers shall bear legal liability according to law.
Article 1229 Where damage is caused to another person by polluting the environment or damaging the ecological environment, the tortfeasor shall bear tort liability.

Article 1230 In a dispute arising from pollution of the environment or damage to the ecological environment, the actor shall bear the burden of adducing evidence regarding the circumstances exempting or mitigating liability as provided by law, and the absence of a causal relationship between its act and the damage.

Article 1231 Where two or more tortfeasors pollute the environment or damage the ecological environment, the degree of liability borne shall be determined based on factors such as the type, concentration, and discharge volume of pollutants, the method, scope, and extent of ecological damage, and the role played by the act in causing the harmful consequences.

Article 1232 Where a tortfeasor intentionally pollutes the environment or damages the ecological environment in violation of the law, causing serious consequences, the aggrieved person shall have the right to claim corresponding punitive damages.

Article 1233 Where environmental pollution or ecological damage is caused by the fault of a third party, the aggrieved person may claim compensation from the tortfeasor or from the third party. After the tortfeasor pays compensation, it shall have the right to seek recourse against the third party.

Article 1234 Where damage is caused to the ecological environment in violation of state regulations, if the ecological environment can be remedied, the authority designated by the state or the organization provided for by law shall have the right to request the tortfeasor to assume the remediation liability within a reasonable time limit. If the tortfeasor fails to remedy the ecological environment within the time limit, the said authority or organization may remedy it on its own or entrust others to do so, and the necessary expenses shall be borne by the tortfeasor.
Article 1236 Where damage is caused to another person by engaging in highly hazardous operations, tort liability shall be borne.

Article 1237 Where damage is caused to another person by a nuclear accident at a civil nuclear facility or involving nuclear materials transported into or out of such facility, the operator of the civil nuclear facility shall bear tort liability; provided, however, that it shall not bear liability if it can prove that the damage was caused by war, armed conflict, riot, or similar circumstances, or was caused intentionally by the victim.

Article 1238 Where damage is caused to another person by a civil aircraft, the operator of the civil aircraft shall bear tort liability; provided, however, that it shall not bear liability if it can prove that the damage was caused intentionally by the victim.

Article 1239 Where damage is caused to another person by the possession or use of highly hazardous substances such as flammable, explosive, highly toxic, highly radioactive, strongly corrosive, or highly pathogenic substances, the possessor or user shall bear tort liability; provided, however, that it shall not bear liability if it can prove that the damage was caused intentionally by the victim or by force majeure. If the aggrieved person is grossly negligent in causing the damage, the liability of the possessor or user may be mitigated.

Article 1240 Where damage is caused to another person by engaging in operations at highly elevated or high-pressure areas, underground excavation activities, or by using high-speed rail transport, the operator shall bear tort liability; provided, however, that it shall not bear liability if it can prove that the damage was caused intentionally by the victim or by force majeure. If the aggrieved person is grossly negligent in causing the damage, the liability of the operator may be mitigated.

Article 1241 If any loss or harm is caused to any other person due to the loss or abandonment of a highly hazardous substance, the owner shall bear tort liability. If the owner has placed the highly hazardous substance under the management of another person, the manager shall bear tort liability; if the owner is at fault, the owner and the manager shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 1242 If any loss or harm is caused to any other person due to the illegal possession of a highly hazardous substance, the illegal possessor shall bear tort liability. If the owner or manager is unable to prove that it has exercised a high degree of care to prevent such illegal possession, the owner or manager shall bear joint and several liability with the illegal possessor.

Article 1243 If any person suffers harm from entering, without permission, an area where highly hazardous activities are conducted or highly hazardous substances are stored, and the manager is able to prove that it has taken sufficient safety measures and fulfilled its duty to give adequate warnings, the manager's liability may be mitigated or exempted.

Article 1244 Where any person bears liability for ultrahazardous activities, if the law provides for a limit on compensation, such provisions shall apply, except where the actor has acted intentionally or with gross negligence.

Article 1245 If any domesticated animal causes harm to any other person, the animal keeper or manager shall bear tort liability; however, if it can be proved that the harm was caused by the intentional act or gross negligence of the infringed person, the liability may be exempted or mitigated.

Article 1246 If any person violates management regulations by failing to take safety measures with respect to an animal and thereby causes harm to any other person, the animal keeper or manager shall bear tort liability; however, if it can be proved that the harm was intentionally caused by the infringed person, the liability may be mitigated.
Article 1247 If any dangerous animal, such as a ferocious dog whose keeping is prohibited, causes harm to any other person, the animal keeper or manager shall bear tort liability.

Article 1248 If any animal in a zoo causes harm to any other person, the zoo shall bear tort liability; however, if it can be proved that it has fulfilled its management duties, it shall not bear tort liability.
Article 1249 If any abandoned or escaped animal causes harm to any other person during the period of abandonment or escape, the original keeper or manager of the animal shall bear tort liability.

Article 1250 If an animal causes harm to any other person due to the fault of a third party, the infringed person may claim compensation from either the animal keeper or manager or from the third party. After the animal keeper or manager has paid compensation, it shall have the right to seek recourse from the third party.
Article 1251 The keeping of animals shall comply with laws and regulations, respect social ethics, and shall not interfere with the life of others.

Article 1252 If a building, structure, or other facility collapses or subsides and causes harm to any other person, the development project owner and the construction unit shall bear joint and several liability, except where the development project owner and the construction unit are able to prove that there is no quality defect. After the development project owner and the construction unit have paid compensation, if there are other persons responsible, they shall have the right to seek recourse from such other persons.
If a building, structure, or other facility collapses or subsides due to reasons attributable to the owner, manager, user, or a third party, thereby causing harm to any other person, the owner, manager, user, or third party shall bear tort liability.

Article 1253 If an object that is detached or falls from a building, structure, or other facility, including any object placed or hung thereon, causes harm to any other person, the owner, manager, or user shall bear tort liability unless it can prove that it is not at fault. After the owner, manager, or user has paid compensation, if there are other persons responsible, it shall have the right to seek recourse from such other persons.

Article 1254 The throwing of objects from a building is prohibited. If any object thrown from a building or falling from a building causes harm to any other person, the tortfeasor shall bear tort liability in accordance with law. If, after investigation, it is difficult to identify the specific tortfeasor, the users of the building who are likely to have caused the harm shall provide compensation, unless they can prove that they are not the tortfeasor. After having provided compensation, the users of the building who are likely to have caused the harm shall have the right to seek recourse from the tortfeasor.
Property service enterprises and other building managers shall take necessary security measures to prevent the occurrence of the circumstances described in the preceding paragraph; if they fail to take necessary security measures, they shall bear tort liability for failing to fulfill safety guarantee obligations in accordance with law.
In the event of the circumstances set forth in the first paragraph of this Article, the public security authorities and other relevant authorities shall investigate promptly in accordance with law to ascertain the person responsible.

Article 1255 If any piled object collapses, rolls, or slides and causes harm to any other person, the person who piled the object shall bear tort liability unless it can prove that it is not at fault.

Article 1256 If any person stacks, dumps, or spills objects that obstruct traffic on a public road, thereby causing harm to any other person, the person who committed the act shall bear tort liability. If the manager of the public road is unable to prove that it has fulfilled its obligations of cleaning, protection, warning, or the like, it shall bear corresponding liability.

Article 1257 If any harm is caused to any other person due to the breaking, toppling, or falling of fruits of trees or the like, the owner or manager of the tree shall bear tort liability unless it can prove that it is not at fault.

Article 1258 If any person excavates, repairs, or installs underground facilities or the like in a public place or on a road, thereby causing harm to any other person, the person carrying out the construction shall bear tort liability unless it can prove that it has set up clear signs and taken safety measures.
If any underground facility such as a manhole cover causes harm to any other person, the manager shall bear tort liability unless it can prove that it has fulfilled its management duties.
Supplementary Provisions

Article 1259 The terms “or above,” “or below,” “within,” and “expiration of” as used in civil law include the number itself; the terms “less than,” “more than,” and “outside,” as used in civil law do not include the number itself.

Article 1260 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2021. The Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of Succession of the People's Republic of China, the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Adoption Law of the People's Republic of China, the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, and the General Provisions of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China shall be repealed simultaneously.
